I was always interested in guerrilla theater, I studied it in a playwriting class in school. But this was really a last resort. I had been going to meetings for months, and I have a lot of sympathy for these representatives, because I am the vice chair of my local planning group. I know what it’s like to sit there and get dunked on by random people. So, I did my homework on all of them. I learned what they voted for, what they've voted against, the progressive policies that they had enacted that I could support. I went so far as to bring them flowers.
But at a certain point, it felt like we've exhausted all of the efforts. We did it the right way, and they still continued to ignore their constituents.
I was in the shower one day and it hit me. I was trying to think of how I could satirize their points, because I realized they seemed to have a lack of self-awareness. I realized we're not getting through to them, and they are not listening to us and there's no consequences for them not listening to us. So, maybe we need to show them how silly they're being.
How did you prepare?
I am a huge Star Wars fan. I used to watch the movies almost every day as a kid. In the lead-up to the meeting, I rewatched all the movies again, the original ones, trying to get his gesticulations down. I got a silk cape, I think it was from Turkey. I found the original 2004 Hasbro helmet, and I chose this one because it had a voice changer in it. But I had been told the voice changer was a little bit gimmicky, so I thought “I'll just replicate his voice myself.” I wasn’t able to get everything I wanted for the costume, but I knew that the August 19th meeting was going to be the big one, because the ACLU was going to be at that committee meeting. So I pulled together some stuff I already had, and I think it turned out well.
The helmet actually came in handy, because there were buttons on it to make noises. At certain points, I'd stand up to go to the bathroom and I'd hit the breathing button—you know, the Darth Vader breathing sound. At one point I turned around, and I'm right within earshot of the chief of police, and I pushed the button and it said, “Your powers are weak!”
What do you hope this achieves?
I want to make it cool to engage in one's civic responsibility again. City council meetings don't have to be stale rooms with boring thoughts presented in unoriginal ways. They can be places where we bring our own art, where we bring the strength of our intellect and our moral fortitude with our talent and creativity.
This sparked a global conversation about luxury surveillance and living under Big Brother, and in Orwellian-digital, fully surveilled hellscape. Some people didn't know what Flock was a week ago. We've reframed the narrative from “this is a ‘necessary evil’” to “If Darth Vader finds it a ‘necessary evil,’ that should make us pause and reflect on whether or not we need it.”

articles.title: Stability AI, maker of image generator Stable Diffusion, raises $76 million in fresh funding | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Stability AI, the startup behind AI image generation model Stable Diffusion, has raised $76 million in Series B funding. The new haul brings the company’s fundraising total to $232 million.
The company announced the round Tuesday, saying the new capital comes partly from a number of prominent entertainment industry organizations, including Universal Music Group, Sony Music Group, Warner Music Group, and gaming giant Electronic Arts (EA). Two investment firms, AMD Ventures and Pacific Alliance Ventures, also took part.
It’s an unusual roster and a less typical venture round than a lineup of the companies Stability now depends on for content licensing and distribution deals.
Stability AI CEO Prem Akkaraju, who joined the company in 2024, called the funding “an affirmation of our vision where generative AI empowers every producer, musician, and storyteller.”
The company says it plans to use the money from its latest funding round to continue building out its “creative production” product suite while also expanding its professional services arm. Currently, Stability offers a variety of AI models that are designed for the purposes of AI music, video, and image generation.
Stability, founded in 2019, has spent the past year signing deals to weave generative AI into entertainment companies’ creative workflows. It struck partnerships with Universal Music and EA last October and with Warner Music last November, each giving those companies a hand in co-developing Stability’s AI tools rather than just licensing the output..
Stability has also had a mostly winning stretch in court. The company largely prevailed in a copyright lawsuit brought by Getty Images in the United Kingdom, which had accused the company of infringing upon IP rights by using the company’s images in the training of its image generation model. A judge ruled largely in Stability’s favor in that case, but a similar lawsuit from Getty in the U.S. is still working its way through the courts.
Stability was also sued in 2023 by the company’s co-founder, Cyrus Hodes, who claimed that he was tricked by the other co-founder, Emad Mostaque, into selling his share in the company.

articles.title: Instagram adds feature that automatically trims clips for Reels - Engadget
articles.text:
Instagram adds feature that automatically trims clips for Reels
First Draft takes care of the busywork of video editing.
Meta is adding a new feature to Instagram that should make it easier to edit short-form videos. The feature, called First Draft, can automatically trim silences and pauses from clips, letting the bulk of your editing time focus on making creative decisions rather than cleaning up videos.
To use First Draft, Instagram says you just need to select clips from your Reels Gallery and tap "First Draft." The feature then analyzes your clips, trims them appropriately and then lays your clips out in a timeline where you can play them back. From there, you can edit them further in the app or post them straight to your feed or Story. Meta says you'll also be able to use First Drafts immediately after you shoot new footage on Instagram.
Meta launched Edits, a standalone video editing app, in April 2025, with a variety of AI-powered editing features that were supposed to make Reels easier to produce. AI isn't mentioned at all in the company's announcement of First Draft, and that's apparently because the feature doesn't use the technology, The Verge reports. That might be because Meta technically classifies First Draft as "machine learning" rather than AI, but it's still a notable change for Instagram.
As of late, the photo and video sharing app has been home to all sorts of different AI experiments, from Meta's decision to force Meta AI into Instagram messages to a feature that lets you prompt Instagram to edit your Stories for you. None have felt particularly necessary for the core experience of posting things, which makes First Draft's utility stand out.
Meta says First Draft will be available on iOS first, and hasn't shared when the feature will come to Android.

articles.title: Kefine ra mắt tai nghe rẻ nhất của mình, chất lượng còn đáng để tin cậy?
articles.text:
Có mức giá chỉ dưới 1 triệu đồng, Kefine Loric có xứng đáng để tâm hay chúng ta nên bỏ thêm tiền để chọn các sản phẩm cao cấp hơn?
Sau sự ra mắt của tai nghe đầu bảng Kefine Arnar và sản phẩm kế nhiệm cho dòng Klean, Kefine tiếp tục trở lại thị trường với cặp tai nghe có mức giá rẻ nhất của họ từ trước đến nay mang tên Kefine Loric.
Hãng giới thiệu khá nhiều về việc đây là một tai nghe dù nằm ở tầm giá rẻ vẫn đem lại chất lượng âm thanh tốt nhờ vào màng loa được phủ Titanium. Thực tế có đúng với quảng cáo hay không?
Hộp của các sản phẩm Kefine vẫn luôn đơn giản với chỉ hình sản phẩm và công nghệ màng loa được sử dụng.
Bộ phụ kiện của tai nghe nằm ở mức cao bản, bao gồm một túi đựng giả da, 6 bộ tips cao su (3 bộ ống hẹp tăng trầm, 3 bộ ống rộng tăng âm cao) cùng với sợi dây kết nối.
Dây của Loric vẫn được làm dưới dạng 2-pin thông dụng, có thêm microphone để đàm thoại và cắm cổng 3.5mm. Lỗi bên trong được làm bằng dây đồng mạ bạc 160 sợi.
Đối với những bạn thường xuyên chơi game hoặc thường xuyên phải họp online, cần chất lượng đàm thoại tốt thì hãng cũng có một sợi dây rời...
... dây này sử dụng cổng USB-C, và có thiết kế khá đặc biệt...
... khi mà cổng cắm 2-pin được tách ra làm 2 phần, có thể cắm thêm microphone dạng boom như thế này. Mic dạng boom sẽ được đưa tới gần miệng hơn, giúp cho tiếng nói của người dùng rõ hơn so với chiếc mic được tích hợp trên dây.
Trở lại với tai nghe, Loric nằm ở tầm giá rẻ nên việc nó được hoàn thiện hoàn toàn bằng nhựa đúc cũng không có gì mà bất ngờ cả. Mặt ngoài của tai nghe được làm khá đơn giản, chỉ có độc một màu xám bạc, kèm một đường nổi ở chính giữa để tạo điểm nhấn nhỏ mà thôi.
Mặt trong tai nghe thì được làm trong suốt hoàn toàn, cho ta thấy được màng loa Dynamic 10mm phủ PU + Titanium ở bên trong.
Dù ở tầm giá rẻ nhưng Kefine vẫn để ý tới những chi tiết nhỏ, như việc hãng in tên sản phẩm và ký hiệu trái phải ở cạnh bên, hay những đường dây ở bên trong đều được đặt một cách gọn gàng.
Chỉ được trang bị cấu hình đơn giản với một màng loa, Loric có kích thước rất "tí hon" so với những cặp tai nghe có nhiều màng loa hiện nay. Nhờ đó, tai nghe khi đặt lên tai thì gần như "biến mất" luôn, cho cảm giác đeo thoải mái kể cả với những bạn nữ có vành tai nhỏ.
Nhìn một cách tổng thể thì cặp tai nghe này có chất lượng hoàn thiện ở mức ổn, không có chi tiết thiết kế hay vật liệu gì đột phá cả nhưng cũng không tạo cảm giác quá rẻ tiền.
Chất âm V-shape đặc trưng của tầm tiền
Thiết bị sử dụng: iPhone 16 Pro > Tanchjim Space II > Kefine Loric
Trong tầm giá dưới 1 triệu đồng, đa phần các thương hiệu âm thanh sẽ nhắm tới kiểu âm V-shape, tăng âm lượng ở dải thấp cũng như dải cao lên để tạo ra sự sôi động trong bài nhạc. Kefine Loric cũng đi theo hướng âm này, hướng tới những bạn thích nhạc Dance, Pop và muốn "nhảy theo nhịp nhạc".
Tai nghe có lượng âm trầm dày dặn, lượng nhiều hơn trung bình một cách rõ rệt. Giống với đa phần những cặp tai nghe với màng loa Dynamic khác, Loric sẽ có một kiểu trầm trải đều từ những tần số thấp nhất (sub-bass) và cả mid-bass luôn, nên việc nó hơi lấn chiếm vị trí thể hiện của giọng ca sĩ cũng là điều không thể tránh khỏi được.
Nghe bài Gangsta's Paradise của Coolio, mỗi tiếng trống đập xuống đều có lực mạnh mẽ, nổi tròn trịa lên khá gần với người nghe. Khả năng tách lớp của dải này nằm ở mức trung bình, khi mà nổi lên thì trống sẽ có xu hướng tràn vào nền (bloom) một chút, chứ không ngắt ngay và luôn.
Vẫn như thường lệ, trong chất âm V-shape thì phần dải trung sẽ không phải là thành phần được chú trọng nhất. Giọng ca sĩ, những tiếng piano hay violin sẽ được giữ ở mức đủ tự nhiên, hơi ngả tối và sẽ lùi về phía sau một chút chứ không đứng ngay trước mặt người nghe. Đây cũng sẽ là điều dễ hiểu trong những cặp tai nghe hướng tới sự sôi động như Loric, việc đẩy mạnh 2 dải âm còn lại cũng sẽ khiến giọng ca sĩ phải nhường lại vị trí thể hiện.
Trong bài Crazy của Gnarls Barkley, giọng nam ca sĩ gần như là đứng ngang hàng với những tiếng trống phía sau. Phần trung cao (high-mid) được làm nhẹ lại, không cao được tới những tần số cuối cùng, nhờ đó mà hiện tượng chói (sibilance) rất ít khi xảy ra, ngược lại thì giọng ca sĩ nữ như Laura Pausini cũng không sáng và "thoát" được hẳn khỏi nền âm phía dưới.
Với chất âm V-shape, Loric lại tiếp tục tăng năng lượng trở lại khi lên tới dải cao (treble), đáng nói nhất là 1 đoạn đẩy sáng ở 8KHz rất đặc trưng của những tai nghe dạng Dynamic. Tổng thể thì đây vẫn là một cặp tai nghe thiên về độ đậm, nên dải cao này vẫn có phần "lép vế" hơn so với những tiếng trống ở phía dưới, song vẫn làm được nhiệm vụ giữ chất âm của Loric không bị quá tối.
Như thường lệ, những cặp tai nghe ở tầm giá dưới 1 triệu thì cũng sẽ có tính kỹ thuật trong chất âm ở mức vừa phải thôi. Khả năng bóc tách những chi tiết nhỏ hay độ rộng âm thanh (âm trường) không thể so sánh được với các tai nghe cao cấp hơn của hãng như Kefine Klean SV hay Arnar được.
Cặp tai nghe hướng tới sự sôi động
Nhìn một cách tổng thể, Kefine Loric là một cặp tai nghe dành cho những bạn kiếm tìm một chất âm V-shape sôi động, phục vụ cho việc nghe những bài nhạc Dance, Pop, EDM mà không cần phải bỏ ra một số tiền quá nhiều. Chất lượng hoàn thiện của tai nghe cũng nằm ở mức ổn trong tầm giá, có sự chỉn chu trong thiết kế, vật liệu cho tới những phụ kiện kèm theo.
Tuy vậy, đây sẽ không phải là cặp tai nghe để hướng tới những bạn thích dòng nhạc cổ điển hay Vocals, Jazz. Phần dải trung của cặp tai nghe này vì đã phải nhường chỗ cho những dải âm khác nên không thực sự nổi bật. Kèm theo đó là khả năng tách lớp những chi tiết nhỏ hay âm trường sẽ không theo kịp được với những bài nhạc nhiều nhạc cụ với cấu trúc phức tạp.

articles.title: The Best Early Labor Day Kitchen Deals for Busy Fall Days
articles.text:
Nights are feeling crisp, it's getting darker earlier, and kids are back at school—for most people, vacation meals and casual picnics are over, and it's time to get back to business with meal and menu prep. If you're dusting off your pots, pans, and air fryers and thinking you could use an upgrade, Labor Day is a great time to score deals on appliances and cookware. Though the deals aren't quite as good as Prime Day's or Black Friday's, they're still substantial. These are the best early discounts I've found on gear the WIRED Reviews team has tested, loves, and uses in their own kitchens.
Check out our other early Labor Day deals on tech gadgets, as well as our kitchen coverage.
Featured Deals
All-Clad Mother of All Pans for $150 ($150 Off)
All-Clad is having a sale on many cookware sets and devices, but if you're going to get just one pan, this should be it. You can't beat All-Clad's durability and lifetime warranty, and WIRED kitchen reviewer Matthew Korfhage likes this 6-quart model specifically because it has the broadest surface of any of All-Clad's stainless steel pans, at over 11 inches. It also has a lid and is oven- and broiler-safe up to 600 degrees Fahrenheit. I can personally attest to the All-Clad quality, as I've had the D3 sauté pan since 2005, and it still looks nearly new.
Cuisinart Air Fryer Oven and Grill for $158 ($62 Off)
The best air fryer deal on a model we recommend is this combination air fryer/toaster oven from Cuisinart, which WIRED reviewer Matthew Korfhage loves for its ability to crisp, broil, toast, and even grill on a little George Foreman-style griddle. The interior isn't the easiest to clean, but unlike many air fryers, it is compact enough to fit comfortably on most countertops—15.75 inches wide by 12.25 inches deep by 13.75 inches high.
Keurig K-Cafe Smart Single-Serve Coffee Maker for $100 ($100 Off)
Everyone knows this is not the best way to make great-tasting coffee—we have other machines we recommend for that. But if you live by yourself and just need a quick cup in the middle of the day, or want something simple and unfussy for the office, you really can't beat this half-off deal. WIRED reviewer Louryn Strampe tested this model at her house and praised its built-in milk frother; BrewID, which identifies an inserted pod and suggests settings for brewing it (or, in the app, recipes to use); and MultiStream technology, which saturates the pod grounds for a better cup.
Anova Sous Vide Precision Cooker 3.0 for $169 ($60 Off)
Not only is an immersion circulator a great way to slow-cook lean meats, but it's also a way to home-pasteurize your eggs to ensure they're salmonella-free. I love this Anova model because the touchscreen makes it easy for anyone to use—just clip it onto a pot filled with water, select your temperature on the touchscreen, and cook away.
Instant Pot Pro Plus for $170 ($60 Off)
I have an older model of this particular Instant Pot model, which WIRED reviewer Joe Ray gave an 8/10, and it's one of the most-used appliances in my home. If you're looking to simplify your meal prep during the busy fall school-and-sports season, this is the way. It will cook dried beans and tough meats in just a fraction of the time it would take via other methods, and if you haven't tried any of the internet's legion of Instant Pot-specific recipes, you should. They will probably surprise you.
KitchenAid 5-Quart Artisan Stand Mixer for $349 ($119 Off)
If you're looking to get a jump on fall or holiday baking, you can grab KitchenAid's timeless tilt-head Artisan model for Prime Day prices right now. Only certain colors are on sale at Walmart, but if you don't see something you like, QVC has a bigger selection for just $30 more.

articles.title: Free accounts can now access ChatGPT's upgraded task scheduling tool - Engadget
articles.text:
Free accounts can now access ChatGPT's upgraded task scheduling tool
Meanwhile, paid accounts can configure prompts to trigger when things happen in Gmail, Slack or GitHub.
Back in June, OpenAI added a dedicated section within ChatGPT's sidebar to highlight the fact could you schedule prompts through its chatbot. The company also introduced enhancements to ChatGPT's ability to complete tasks in the future, making it easier to track and edit those requests. At the time, the new hub, alongside the expanded scheduling features that came with it, was only available to Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise customers. Now, even those with free accounts can access the scheduling menu.
At the same time, OpenAI has made it possible to share scheduled tasks with other users, so that if you think of a clever use of the feature, others can benefit from it for their own workflows. And if you're a paid subscriber, you can now configure ChatGPT to trigger a prompt as things happen in Gmail, Slack and GitHub. OpenAI is making this feature available to Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise users starting today.
OpenAI suggests a few different use cases for scheduled tasks. For instance, you can set up travel alerts related to an upcoming trip, or tell ChatGPT to notify you of new movies and TV shows as they're added to your favorite streaming services. Selfishly, you could also tell the chatbot to summarize the latest news from Engadget each morning, but be a pal and make sure to click through to read the links.

articles.title: SpaceX will build a second, $100B 'Starbase' spaceport in Louisiana | TechCrunch
articles.text:
SpaceX has announced it will build a second spaceport for future launches of its Starship mega-rocket at a former Exxon property in Louisiana, ending what the company says was a seven-year search for a suitable location.
The new launch site will sit along the Gulf Coast in Vermilion Parish, west of New Orleans and roughly 10 hours from the company’s existing Starbase complex in South Texas. SpaceX says it is investing $100 billion, with construction starting in 2027. SpaceX claims the first Starship launch will take place in 2029.
Louisiana Economic Development (LED), the state agency that oversees business development, offers a slightly more conservative timeline. It says construction will start by the end of 2027 with “initial operations expected to come online in 2030.”
Before any of that happens, SpaceX is still trying to prove that it can fly Starship into low-Earth orbit and make the rocket reusable, like its existing Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets. SpaceX has performed 13 test flights of Starship since 2023, and while the company has ticked off a lot of development boxes, it still has a lot of work to do.
An upcoming 14th test flight could see SpaceX send Starship’s upper stage to orbit for the first time. But the company has yet to return both the booster and the upper stage to the launch pad on a single flight, a basic necessity if Starship is to become truly reusable. Even then, SpaceX must show that it can bring the vehicle back and refurbish it quickly enough to reach its own aggressive goal of sending up multiple Starships per week.
That isn’t stopping SpaceX from betting almost everything on Starship. This past week, SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk said he will retire the Falcon rockets once Starship is flying multiple times per week. His comments confirmed earlier reporting from Bloomberg News that the company was already telling prospective customers about the impending end of the Falcon program.
SpaceX has spent more than $8 billion developing Starship, according to filings submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission. The rocket — which is the largest and most powerful ever built — is crucial to maintaining and growing the only profitable part of SpaceX’s business, its Starlink satellite internet service. SpaceX is also planning to build an entire network of satellites dedicated to AI processing, which it needs Starship to launch.
The new Starbase site will create 3,000 direct new jobs over 10 years, with an average annual salary of $92,600, according to LED. More than 30,000 construction jobs are expected at the peak of the buildout.
It’s not immediately clear if SpaceX intends to create a company town around the new Starbase site, like the one it has architected in Texas. The Texas municipality, once called Boca Chica and renamed Starbase, has its own ZIP code and volunteer fire station, and is building its own police force and community library. It is run by a local government filled with SpaceX employees (or family members of SpaceX employees).
SpaceX did say in its announcement that it wants to make the new site a “self-sustaining spaceport” with “propellant production, power generation, deep-water shipping capabilities, vehicle processing facilities, and an airport.”
As a mix of a launch complex and active construction zone, the Starbase site in Texas has also seen extremely high injury rates over the last decade. It’s the most dangerous site SpaceX operates and the company has reported hundreds of injuries to the Occupational Health and Safety Administration. In May, a construction worker employed by a third-party contractor fell to his death at Starbase.
“We are very excited to be in this position to receive one of the best opportunities of a lifetime which will bring not only a variety of jobs to our Parish but will offer opportunities to our grandchildren allowing them to stay home for employment,” Vermilion Parish Police Jury President Chad Vallo said in a statement.
SpaceX, which has for years faced criticism for — and fought legal battles over — how it treats the local ecosystem around its Texas site, has “already engaged the Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries, Coastal Protection and Restoration Authority and other appropriate state agencies to proactively address potential impacts to wildlife, fisheries and their supporting habitats,” according to LED.
The company also says it is “partnering with state and federal agencies to expand Louisiana’s Coastal Master Plan and Coastal Wetlands Planning, Protection and Restoration Act projects, including Gulf shoreline protection breakwaters designed to reduce wave energy” and reduce shoreline erosion in the area.

articles.title: Xiaomi giới thiệu loạt chip mới, không chỉ cho smartphone: Có cả tiến trình 3nm, mở rộng sang AI và xe tự lái
articles.text:
Xiaomi đang mở rộng tham vọng bán dẫn vượt khỏi smartphone, với loạt chip mới trải từ SoC 3nm cho điện thoại đến tăng tốc AI và xe tự lái.
Xiaomi đang mở rộng chiến lược tự phát triển chip ra ngoài smartphone khi cùng lúc giới thiệu ba dòng chip XRING mới cho điện thoại, AI và xe tự lái. Đáng chú ý, hai trong số này được sản xuất trên tiến trình 3 nm, trong khi chip còn lại được thiết kế riêng để tăng tốc các mô hình AI lớn.
Chip 3 nm đạt hơn 5,2 triệu điểm AnTuTu
Trong ba chip mới, XRING O3 là sản phẩm gần với người dùng phổ thông nhất. Đây là SoC dành cho smartphone, được sản xuất trên tiến trình 3 nm của TSMC và dự kiến lần đầu xuất hiện trên Xiaomi 18 Fold, mẫu điện thoại màn hình gập dự kiến ra mắt tại Trung Quốc vào tháng 9.
Theo số liệu do Xiaomi công bố, XRING O3 đạt 5.228.014 điểm trong thử nghiệm AnTuTu nội bộ. Chip được trang bị CPU 10 nhân và GPU 16 nhân. So với thế hệ trước, Xiaomi cho biết hiệu năng CPU tăng 60%, hiệu năng đồ họa tăng 85%, trong khi hiệu quả năng lượng cải thiện 64%.
XRING O3 cũng hỗ trợ bộ nhớ LPDDR6 với băng thông tối đa 113,8 GB/s. Khả năng xử lý AI đạt khoảng 200 TOPS, còn động cơ mạng nơ-ron nhanh hơn 45% so với thế hệ trước.
Xiaomi cho biết hãng mất 459 ngày để phát triển XRING O3. Ngoài Xiaomi 18 Fold, chip này dự kiến được trang bị trên Pad 9 Pro Max.
Tuy nhiên, việc Xiaomi tự thiết kế chip chưa đồng nghĩa hãng sẽ lập tức thay thế Qualcomm và MediaTek. Công ty cho biết vẫn sẽ sử dụng phần lớn chip của hai nhà cung cấp này cho smartphone, đồng thời từng bước mở rộng chip tự thiết kế trên một số dòng sản phẩm chủ lực.
Từ smartphone sang chip AI
Nếu XRING O3 cho thấy Xiaomi muốn kiểm soát nhiều hơn công nghệ cốt lõi bên trong smartphone, XRING O100 lại cho thấy tham vọng đã mở rộng sang một lĩnh vực hoàn toàn khác.
O100 là bộ tăng tốc AI được sản xuất trên tiến trình 6 nm, sử dụng kiến trúc xếp chồng bộ xử lý và bộ nhớ theo chiều dọc. Thiết kế này nhằm rút ngắn khoảng cách giữa bộ nhớ và bộ xử lý, qua đó giảm độ trễ khi chạy các mô hình AI lớn.
Theo Xiaomi, O100 đạt băng thông tối đa 1,22 TB/s. Chip được thiết kế cho các mô hình AI chạy trực tiếp trên thiết bị, với phạm vi ứng dụng từ smartphone, máy tính đến robot và ôtô.
Trong thử nghiệm của Xiaomi, hệ thống sử dụng O100 đạt tốc độ suy luận tối đa 330 token/giây dành cho mô hình 3 tỷ tham số, và khả năng chạy cục bộ các mô hình AI tới 120 tỷ tham số. Con số này phản ánh điều kiện thử nghiệm cụ thể của hãng, không phải tốc độ áp dụng cho mọi mô hình AI.
O100 đã hoàn tất quá trình kiểm chứng silicon và dự kiến được thương mại hóa từ năm 2027.
Xiaomi cũng sử dụng O100 trong AI Cube Prototype để trình diễn khả năng chạy mô hình AI cục bộ. Tuy nhiên, đây mới chỉ là nguyên mẫu và chưa phải sản phẩm thương mại, mặc dù vậy, sự xuất hiện của AI Cube trong sự kiện lần này cho thấy cách Xiaomi có thể kết hợp các chip XRING trong một hệ thống AI.
D100 đưa Xiaomi vào cuộc đua chip xe tự lái
Mảnh ghép thứ ba là XRING D100, chip tính toán AI dành cho hệ thống lái thông minh.
D100 được sản xuất trên tiến trình 3 nm, sở hữu CPU 20 nhân và NPU 16 nhân, đồng thời hỗ trợ tối đa 160 GB bộ nhớ hợp nhất. Xiaomi cho biết chip có thể vận hành các mô hình AI lớn với quy mô tới 200 tỷ tham số.
Hãng đã hoàn tất quá trình kiểm chứng D100, nhưng chip dự kiến chỉ được ứng dụng trên xe thực tế từ năm 2027. Xiaomi hiện chưa công bố hiệu năng TOPS của D100 cũng như mẫu xe đầu tiên sử dụng chip này.
Sự xuất hiện của D100 đáng chú ý bởi Xiaomi đang bước vào một thị trường mà nhiều hãng xe điện Trung Quốc đã tự phát triển chip lái thông minh. Nio, Li Auto, Xpeng và BYD đều đã có những nỗ lực riêng trong lĩnh vực này.
Như vậy, ba chip mới đang mở ra ba hướng ứng dụng khác nhau: O3 cho smartphone, O100 cho AI và D100 cho xe tự lái. Đây cũng là dấu hiệu cho thấy Xiaomi không còn xem năng lực thiết kế chip chỉ là công cụ để tạo khác biệt cho điện thoại.
Xiaomi đã đầu tư hơn 21 tỷ nhân dân tệ vào chip
Chiến lược bán dẫn của Xiaomi không bắt đầu với ba chip mới. Công ty cho biết kể từ khi tái khởi động chương trình phát triển chip vào năm 2021, hãng đã đầu tư hơn 21 tỷ nhân dân tệ và xây dựng đội ngũ khoảng 3.000 kỹ sư.
Trước XRING O3, Xiaomi đã phát triển XRING O1 cho smartphone. Tổng số thiết bị xuất xưởng sử dụng O1 đã vượt 1 triệu máy, nhưng số smartphone bán ra kể từ sau tháng 5/2025 mới đạt khoảng 150.000 máy.
Những con số này cho thấy Xiaomi vẫn đang ở giai đoạn đầu của quá trình mở rộng chip tự thiết kế. Hãng chưa thể ngay lập tức thay thế các nhà cung cấp chip bên ngoài trên smartphone, cũng chưa thể chuyển toàn bộ hệ thống tính toán trên xe sang chip nội bộ.
Thay vào đó, Xiaomi đang xây dựng từng mảnh của một hệ sinh thái bán dẫn riêng. Chip smartphone, chip tăng tốc AI và chip lái thông minh có thể trở thành những nền tảng tính toán phục vụ nhiều sản phẩm khác nhau, từ điện thoại đến robot và ôtô.
Thách thức không chỉ nằm ở công nghệ
Tự thiết kế chip giúp Xiaomi có thêm quyền kiểm soát đối với công nghệ, đồng thời có thể giảm sự phụ thuộc vào các nhà cung cấp bên ngoài và tăng khả năng khác biệt hóa sản phẩm. Tuy nhiên, đây cũng là chiến lược đòi hỏi nguồn vốn lớn và thời gian dài trước khi tạo ra hiệu quả thương mại rõ rệt.
Trong ba tháng tính đến tháng 6/2026, Xiaomi ghi nhận khoản lỗ hoạt động 2,6 tỷ nhân dân tệ ở các mảng kinh doanh mới như xe điện và AI. Trong khi đó, O100 và D100 đều phải tới năm 2027 mới dự kiến được thương mại hóa rộng hơn.
Vì vậy, thử thách lớn nhất với Xiaomi không chỉ là tạo ra những con chip có thông số ấn tượng. Hãng còn phải chứng minh chúng có thể được sản xuất ở quy mô lớn, tích hợp vào sản phẩm thực tế và tạo ra hiệu quả kinh tế đủ để bù đắp khoản đầu tư.
Ba chip XRING mới vì thế chưa cho thấy Xiaomi đã thoát khỏi sự phụ thuộc vào Qualcomm, MediaTek hay Nvidia. Nhưng chúng cho thấy phạm vi tham vọng bán dẫn của hãng đang thay đổi rõ rệt: từ việc tự phát triển chip cho smartphone sang xây dựng nền tảng tính toán cho AI, robot và xe tự lái.

articles.title: Google’s Pixel 11 Pro Fold Is Better, but Not the Best
articles.text:
Good camera. Slightly improved design. IP68 water and dust resistance. Qi2 25W wireless charging. Slick AI features and software.
TIRED
Significantly weaker specs than other Pro models. Comparatively chunky. $100 more than last year’s 10 Pro Fold.
The Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold is a predictably iterative improvement over last year’s foldable, with slight upgrades to performance and the camera, but it comes with an unwelcome $100 price bump. The IP68 rating for water and dust resistance and the Qi2 25W support for faster magnetic charging are standouts in a category where Google is lagging, but it has never been known for its hardware. Software is where the company excels, and some folks will appreciate the unrivaled AI-infused software features.
Google is good at elevating its devices beyond the spec sheet, but the 11 Pro Fold is perilously close to the Pixel 11 on paper, a phone that’s less than half its price. Beyond the big unfolding screen and customizable rear LEDs, little else justifies the “Pro” tag. With Samsung’s fresh Fold8 form factor and a folding iPhone on the horizon, I’m not convinced Google has done enough to make this the foldable you drop $1,900 on.
Devil in the Details
The Pixel 11 Pro Fold doesn’t look different from the 10 Pro Fold, but Google has shaved off a fraction of a millimeter and 19 grams. Sadly, the 11 Pro Fold is still heavier and thicker (239 grams and 10.1 mm) than Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold8 (201 grams and 9.7 mm), the Fold8 Ultra (215 grams and 8.9 mm), and the Honor Magic V6 (219 grams and 8.75 mm, not sold in the US). That makes it a little trickier to handle, though the horizontal camera bar means less rocking than Samsung’s phones when they lie flat.
The double-camera module has had a makeover, so it looks less chunky, and the back is matte-textured glass that feels lovely. The Pixel 11 Pro Fold scores an impressive IP68 rating for water and dust resistance. That compares favorably to Samsung’s IP48 ratings, which means both can survive shallow submersion, but Google’s phone is dust-tight, whereas Samsung’s phones are at risk from fine dust and sand.
Photograph: Simon Hill
It’s a shame the Fold is only available in two colors: Obsidian, the color of my review unit, looks more like a dark matte gray than black, while Olive Green has a shinier gold frame.
I’m not a fan of Google’s asymmetrical design. With the Pixel 11 Pro Fold closed, there’s a curved corner cutout, and when you open the phone, the two halves have slightly different thicknesses. All folding phones still have a detectable fold line in the middle of the screen when you open them, but Google’s is among the most noticeable. Some folks won’t notice or care, but I’m the kind of guy who goes upstairs to turn the light on so the downstairs switches aren’t misaligned.
The fingerprint sensor in the power button always bugs me when I switch to a folding phone, because I have to pick it up to touch it and unlock the screen, rather than pressing on the screen like most phones. You do have face unlock with the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, and it works well provided there’s ample light, but it still doesn’t work in a dark room, which is still annoying.
You get two lovely, sharp OLED displays in the Pixel 11 Pro Fold: an 8-inch main screen and a 6.5-inch cover screen. Both push peak brightness to 3,600 nits, remaining legible in direct sunlight, and boast a variable refresh rate up to 120 Hz. They’re smooth, with rich colors, and I have nothing to complain about beyond that crease.
Pro Pretender
I’m not convinced the 11 Pro Fold earns the “Pro” in its title. It does have the new HiLight feature, a group of color LEDs in the camera module’s flash that light up different colors based on who is calling, or swirl through the rainbow while you chat to Gemini. It’s neat, if a little underbaked. It’s handy if you put your phone face down when you’re working or trying to relax, but it’s a very minor feature.
All the Pixels get the new Tensor G6 processor, and the Fold has 16 GB of RAM paired with 256 GB, 512 GB, or 1 TB of storage. Switching from the Pixel 10 Pro XL, it was mostly smooth sailing. But it froze a couple of times in split-screen view in Gmail and after launching an app on the outer display, then unfolding the inner display.
The 11 Pro Fold actually has more in common with the regular Pixel 11, because it misses out on the high-end camera in its Pro siblings. Folding phones struggle to match flagships on camera specs because of form-factor limitations, and they must include two front-facing cameras (one for open and one for closed).
Photograph: Simon Hill
You get the same 48-megapixel main camera and 10.8-megapixel telephoto for 5X optical zoom as on the Pixel 11, but the Fold drops to a 10.5-megapixel ultrawide. The main camera is excellent in a wide range of scenarios, and I used the telephoto lens a lot. The 5X zoom produces sharp, detailed shots, though things get a little fuzzy if you push up to the maximum digital zoom capability at 30X. The ultrawide is a very obvious weak spot, producing relatively grainy images, though it doubles as a macro lens for decent, if slightly distorted, close-ups. The 10-megapixel front-facing cameras are passable for selfies.
The 11 Pro and 11 Pro XL cameras are superior across the board (50-MP main, 48-MP ultrawide, 48-MP telephoto, and 42-MP front-facing). They also boast instant Night Sight, 120X digital zoom, and better video capture. That said, I took some great shots with the Pixel 11 Pro Fold; its camera results compare favorably to other foldables, and a good telephoto is more useful than an ultrawide.
I like the new camera tricks: Camera Looks lets you define your preferred style, dictating contrast and colors; Magic Capture makes it easy to get video and photos from an event without focusing on the viewfinder; and Creator Suite will delight content creators with some useful tools, like a built-in teleprompter. You can even use Circle to Search in the camera app to get info on anything you circle without snapping a shot first.
Photograph: Simon Hill
Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold, main camera
Unfortunately, there’s one significant area where the Fold looks amateur, and that’s battery life. The 4,806-mAh battery is smaller than the one in last year’s 10 Pro Fold (5,015 mAh). While that downgrade is mitigated by greater power efficiency in the new Tensor chip, Google suggests 24 hours for the 11 Pro Fold, compared to 30-plus for the other Pixel 11 models.
Photograph: Simon Hill
Compared to a folding phone with a silicon-carbon battery, like the Honor Magic V6, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold lacks stamina, but it shouldn’t be an issue for most folks. The battery lost 6 percent in an hour of video streaming, and an hour of casual gaming claimed 9 percent. It will get you through an average day easily, but when I pushed the Fold with a lot of photography and graphically demanding gaming, I had to engage the battery saver before bedtime.
There’s 30-watt wired charging, but you should definitely embrace Qi2 wireless charging with the Pixel 11 Pro Fold as it tops out at 25 watts and is so much more convenient. The magnets stick firmly and ensure perfect alignment. It’s nice to see Qi2 25W in a folding phone, since many competitors haven’t even adopted it in their regular flagships yet.
Software Save
I’m a big fan of Google’s Pixel-exclusive software features. Call Screen saves me from telemarketers daily; I use Now Playing often to add songs to my playlist, and several new features may just persuade you to board the Pixel train. My colleague Julian Chokkattu talked about Rambler in his Pixel 11 Pro review as a more conversational voice-to-text message-drafting tool. I also like that AI overviews pop up contextually to save you a step, offering a Calendar link when someone texts to suggest a meet-up, for example, though it does mean granting Gemini access.
But one of the most useful new features for the Fold is Bubbles. With this, you can keep a floating circular profile picture from an open chat and open or minimize it with a tap. It’s not a new idea (Facebook Chat Heads did it more than a decade ago), but it lets you get on with other things without leaving the chat, potentially floating above two apps in split-screen mode. It also minimizes to a bar at the bottom right when you’re using the main screen.
With folding phones, people always talk about the ability to watch movies and play games on a big screen, but their real strength is multitasking. Message apps can show the list and a preview simultaneously. You can read a café review and check the location on a map, or watch a movie while you skim your emails.
Photograph: Simon Hill
That said, many apps still aren’t optimized for folding phones, so they can look clownishly big or occasionally obscure buttons. As mentioned, I ran into freezing issues and had to restart apps more than once. Sometimes, when you switch from the cover display to the big screen, it fails to scale up, and you might get a prompt to restart the game for full-screen view, as I did with Bloons TD 6.
Foldable newcomers should also beware of the big black bars. You must rotate the opened Fold for maximum screen viewing, but virtually nothing is made for this weird, almost square aspect ratio. You get more room when browsing something like Netflix, but start a video and you’re not much better off than with a large flagship phone like the Pixel 11 Pro XL.
Games fare a little better, and the 11 Pro Fold is great for titles like Clash of Clans, point-and-click adventures like Machinarium, and tower defense games like Bloons TD 6. It’s also a good option for older games via emulators, but for anything too demanding, like Wuthering Waves or Genshin Impact, you can expect dropped frames galore.
The other reason I find myself unfurling the big screen is to read. For browsing the web, doomscrolling Reddit, or, best of all, reading an ebook, a folding phone is a big step up from a regular phone screen. Whether it’s worth the premium you pay is debatable. It’s a little too easy to forget to use the big screen in daily life.
Photograph: Simon Hill
Photograph: Simon Hill
Folding phones have been around for years, but they still feel a bit gimmicky. For folks who think they’re a tough sell when they can get both a higher-spec flagship phone and a tablet for the price, it’s worth laying hands on one to get a feel for the experience. Foldables may not be an inevitable next step for phones, but there’s a reason they’ve carved out a niche.
The 11 Pro Fold starts at $1,899; that’s $100 more than last year’s 10 Pro Fold, but it doesn’t have a storage bump to soften the blow, as the Google Pixel 11 ($899) does. It also lacks the Pro features you’ll find in the Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL ($1,099 and $1,299). If you’re set on a foldable, the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 and Fold8 Ultra ($1,900 and $2,100) demand consideration, and if you don’t live in the US, check out the Honor Magic V6 ($2,100). There are other options and form factors in our best folding phones, but rumors of a folding iPhone persist, so you might want to wait and see what that looks like.
Simon Hill is a senior writer for WIRED and has been testing and writing about technology for around 20 years. You can find his previous work at Business Insider, Reviewed, TechRadar, Android Authority, USA Today, Digital Trends, and many other places. articles.title: Check out this cool Cyberpunk 2077-edition Commodore 64 - Engadget
articles.text:
Check out this cool Cyberpunk 2077-edition Commodore 64
I have no cause to use one, but I want one.
If there's one company whose vibe totally meshes with the world of Cyberpunk 2077, it's that of Commodore. The home computing pioneer's boxy machines surely inspired the cyberdecks used by all good netrunners back in the day. It's why this tie-up between the new Commodore and CD Projekt Red (CDPR) makes as much sense now as it would have done in 1984... or 2077.
The pair have teamed up to make the Commodore 77, a version of the Commodore 64 Ultimate styled as if it was a relic from Night City itself. Its yellow breadbox case is dinged up and marked with graffiti, there's a metal plate on the function row and half-removed stickers. Even the boot screen has been redesigned to better suit its new dystopian aesthetic. If it wasn't for the etched logo on the front, it would be easy to imagine this as something that fell out of the game.
Fans of 2K77 might be excited to learn it ships with a demo containing an "experience" which "expands the lore of the Cyberpunk universe." The demo was created by Polish C64 group Arise with a soundtrack from chiptune artist LukHash. It'll also ship on an "Arasaka"-design cartridge. Buyers will also find a new custom neon power light, stickers, pins, collectible packaging and a themed spiral-bound user guide.
If you're unfamiliar, Commodore was resurrected by YouTuber Christian "Perifractic" Simpson, with its first product being the 64 Ultimate. It's an FPGA-recreation of the original model with a real keyboard, HDMI, USB and WiFi that's backwards-compatible with original C64 accessories. The new models are even made from the original injection mold tooling, and is available in either its original beige "breadbin" shape or the more Amiga-esque C64C. And, from nothing but looks alone, it looks a damn sight better than TheC64Mini for those looking to tickle their nostalgia glands.
The Commodore 77 is available to pre-order for $377 at Commodore.net, but there's no date yet set on when you'll be able to take ownership.

articles.title: Your vote matters! Decide which Audience Choice sessions will make it to TechCrunch Founder Summit | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Each year, we get a huge influx of applicants to speak at TechCrunch’s events, and this year’s Founder Summit in Boston on November 4 will be no different! We want to thank everyone who applied to take part in our programming and to help share their expertise with the startup community.
After careful review, we have 11 finalists who are vying for four slots within this year’s event agenda, and each one showcases the kind of practical, essential insights that can only be delivered by those who have built, iterated, and succeeded.
You can vote via this link to weigh in on which sessions ultimately make the cut. Submissions will close on September 4. If you’re voting and haven’t already gotten your Founder Summit tickets this year, what are you waiting for?
On November 4 in Boston, you’ll get the chance to learn directly from the experts in intimate, exclusive sessions that can put you ahead of the competition or set you up to play a pivotal role in developing the next era of innovators. We still have discounts running on tickets that can save you up to $100 right here!
With that said, let’s dive into our Disrupt Audience Choice nominees, and remember: The voting takes place via this form, so take a look and then submit your vote!
How to Build Events Strategy Before You Can Afford a Full-Time Events Team
Alexandra Ames: Founder and Chief Event Strategist, Blueprint Lab
Early-stage founders approach events one of two ways: say yes to every opportunity, or avoid them entirely because the ROI feels impossible to justify. Neither is smart. Events can build your audience and credibility before product-market fit but only if you’re strategic about which ones deserve your time and budget. We’ll discuss how to think strategically when resources are tight, including how to maximize ROI from founder events like this one. You’ll leave with frameworks for prioritizing stage-appropriate event investments, tactics for proving value without complex tools, and clarity on when events make sense and when they don’t.
How to Build a “Made in the USA” Hardware Company and Actually Scale It
Hannan Happi: CEO and Co-Founder, Exowatt
Domestic manufacturing is back in the spotlight, but building hardware in the U.S. is still widely seen as too expensive to scale. This session explores how founders can design hardware companies that make “Made in the USA” economically viable from day one. We’ll break down supply chain strategy, cost structure, factory partnerships, and how policy tailwinds like the IRA and CHIPS Act change the equation. Attendees will leave with a practical framework for evaluating when domestic manufacturing can become a competitive advantage — not just a branding decision.
Build Something We Don’t Have a Word for Yet
Andy Tang: Partner, Draper Associates
Pitches that change industries rarely fit existing categories — and most investors will pass on them for exactly that reason. This talk explores why the most fundable startups are often the hardest ones to describe, and what that means for how you build and position yours. Founders will leave with a clearer sense of the difference between a market insight and a market-creating idea, and what it actually takes to get a pattern-matching investor to bet on something genuinely new — before the rest of the world has a name for it.
GraphRAG in Action: Stop Hallucinations with Knowledge Graphs
Shishir Tewar: Head of Enterprise Data Engineering, Procore Technologies
Are messy data sources causing your LLMs to hallucinate? Relational databases struggle to bridge the semantic gap for AI. Learn to build a production-ready GraphRAG pipeline that turns chaotic data into actionable insights. Actionable takeaways: Build an offline pipeline to resolve disjointed datasets into “golden records.” Translate flat records into an interconnected Neo4j knowledge graph. Deploy a secure, local LLM (Ollama) to translate natural language into validated Cypher queries. Give your AI the foundational data structure it needs!
The Enterprise AI Playbook: How to Close L’Oreal and Vodafone Before You Raise a Series A
Merve Kitapci: Managing Partner and CGO, ADIN.AI
Most founders chase product-market fit before landing enterprise clients. We did the opposite. This roundtable covers the exact motion for closing global enterprise accounts at pre-Series A: how to structure the first conversation with a Fortune 500 CMO; why agency partnerships accelerate enterprise sales; how to price with no brand recognition; and what zero organic churn means for your fundraising story. Attendees leave with a repeatable enterprise sales framework, an early-stage AI pricing model, and the three things that make a CMO say yes before legal sees the contract.
Lessons from 20 Years of Bootstrapping an Open Source Business to $50M+
Peter Farkas: CEO, Percona
Building a successful open source company without venture capital is rare — scaling it past $50 million in revenue is even rarer. This talk shares two decades of lessons from growing a commercial open source business from zero to global scale. We’ll cover product-market fit, monetizing open source while keeping the core free, building distributed teams before remote work was mainstream, and creating a repeatable go-to-market engine without outside funding. We’ll also discuss failures, hard lessons, and how to compete against well-funded alternatives while staying bootstrapped. Attendees will leave with practical strategies for scaling sustainably.
Small but Mighty: How AI Lets Lean Teams Outship the Giants
Linden Tibbets: CEO and Co-Founder, IFTTT
The playbook has flipped, and we have lived it firsthand. A five-person team can now outbuild, outship, and outmaneuver companies with 500 engineers. This roundtable gets into the tactical reality of running a lean, AI-powered team: which tools are actually worth your time, how to build workflows that compound instead of bloat, and where most teams are burning cycles on AI that goes nowhere. Walk away knowing how to audit your current stack for speed gaps, which AI-driven growth motions are converting right now, and how to use your small size as an advantage, not an excuse.
The Demo Trap: Why Impressive AI Doesn’t Always Build Real Companies
Jeff Mahler: Co-Founder and CTO, Ambi Robotics
In today’s AI boom, impressive demos can generate headlines, funding, and early excitement, but they rarely prove a real business by themselves. This session explores the gap between prototype performance and real-world deployment, and why many promising AI startups stall before reaching scale. Founders and investors will learn how to evaluate whether AI systems are truly ready for production, the operational and reliability metrics that matter most, and how to build companies that can move beyond hype to durable, real-world impact.
From CentOS to Rocky Linux: Building Movements That Outlast You
Gregory Kurtzer: CEO and Founder, CIQ
Greg Kurtzer helped create CentOS, one of the world’s most widely used operating systems, then founded CIQ and launched Rocky Linux when Red Hat discontinued CentOS. In this session, he shares hard-won lessons from building open source movements and a startup from scratch: why founders must leave ego at the door, then navigate the transition from hiring versatile generalists early, then moving to a team of specialists as you scale. He explains the mistake he almost made by dismissing the value of culture and core values, and what it really takes to build something durable.
The Healthcare AI Companies That Will Actually Matter
Vikram Chaudhery, PhD: CEO and Founder, Genoa Ventures
Most AI healthcare demos look incredible and ship nothing. The companies that will matter in 2026 aren’t the ones with the best models. They’re the ones that get decisions to clinicians in an actionable window and change what doctors actually do for the patient in real clinical workflows. This roundtable digs into what separates investable healthcare AI from expensive science fairs, where agentic systems are creating real value beyond copilots, what founders consistently get wrong before their Series A, and the bar that anyone funding, founding, or joining a healthcare AI company should apply.
How Technical AI Founders Get Into YC, a16z Speedrun, and Raise from Top-Tier VCs
George Bandarian: Founder and General Partner, Untapped Ventures
The best technical founders building in AI and robotics aren’t failing because of their product — they’re failing because they don’t understand what top investors are actually looking for. In this roundtable, early-stage technical founders will work through what YC, a16z speedrun, and top-tier VCs evaluate beyond the deck: founder-market fit signals, why most technical founders need a business counterpart earlier than they think, how to position an autonomous economy company for a lead investor, and what the fundraising process actually looks like before you have traction.

articles.title: The US Just Recorded Its First 2 Measles Deaths This Year
articles.text:
Amid a 35-year high in US measles cases, two people in Pennsylvania have died after contracting the virus, the state’s health department confirmed on Tuesday. They are the first measles-related deaths in the country this year.
Both individuals were unvaccinated residents of Lancaster County in south-central Pennsylvania, which has a large Amish population. The health department said in a statement that it would not be releasing additional information about the individuals to protect their privacy. Pennsylvania has recorded 393 measles cases in 2026 so far, with roughly half of those in Lancaster County. Only Utah and South Carolina have logged more cases this year.
Pennsylvania governor Josh Shapiro called measles a “serious and growing problem” across the country in a press conference on Tuesday. “Illness and death from measles is completely preventable,” he said. “We already have the tools to protect ourselves and our families from this disease, which is one of the most contagious diseases on the face of the Earth.”
In Pennsylvania, nearly 20 percent of those infected with measles have been hospitalized. The virus can cause severe complications such as pneumonia, which is the leading cause of death in children who get measles. The infection can also cause brain swelling, or encephalitis, which can sometimes lead to deafness or intellectual disability.
Nationwide, there have been nearly 2,800 measles cases this year, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. That’s up from 2,289 cases in 2025 and well above the 285 cases seen in 2023.
Declining vaccination rates across the country are fueling the current outbreaks. New data released by the CDC earlier this month found that vaccination coverage among kindergartners during the past school year decreased for all reported vaccines. Meanwhile, the number of parents seeking non-medical exemptions for vaccines for their children grew from 3.6 percent to a record high of 4.2 percent nationwide. Measles is so contagious that 95 percent of a community needs to be vaccinated to prevent outbreaks. In Lancaster County, just 87 percent of all incoming kindergarteners are fully vaccinated.
Shapiro cited misinformation around vaccination as a main driver of cases in Pennsylvania. The measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine is 97 percent effective against measles if both doses are given, and serious side effects are extremely rare in fully vaccinated people.
Shapiro said staff at the state health department have held 91 pop-up vaccination clinics and administered more than 4,100 vaccines across the state this year in response to the outbreak. About a quarter of those have been given in Lancaster County.
Health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who has promoted vaccine skepticism and sought to overhaul the childhood vaccination schedule, said on CNN recently that the places facing measles outbreaks are “almost all religious communities that just don’t vaccinate.”
Shapiro noted on Tuesday that measles has been traced to 28 different counties throughout Pennsylvania and said it would not be fair to conclude that this is a problem in one particular community.
The governor said he was late to the press conference because Kennedy called him to offer help in responding to the outbreak. “I was very, very blunt with him,” Shapiro said, noting he turned Kennedy down. “I made very clear that his actions and the rhetoric that's coming from this administration are having a negative impact on communities across America.”
Amid surging measles cases, President Donald Trump recently signed an executive order to “break up” the combined MMR vaccine. Currently, the vaccine involves a two-dose regimen, and splitting up the vaccine could require a total of six visits to the doctor to complete the full vaccine series. More than 210 medical organizations and patient groups issued a statement saying the move would leave children less protected and families more confused. The MMR vaccine has been licensed since 1971 as a single injection, and there is no scientific basis for separating it into separate vaccines.

articles.title: Thông tin quan trọng đến tất cả người dùng iPhone
articles.text:
Một thay đổi nhỏ trong cách sử dụng iPhone có thể tạo ra khác biệt lớn với người dùng.
Với nhiều người dùng iPhone, thiết bị này là công cụ được sử dụng xuyên suốt từ lúc bắt đầu ngày mới cho đến khi đi ngủ.
Sự phụ thuộc đó càng trở nên rõ ràng khi chiếc iPhone sắp hết pin nhưng người dùng chưa thể tìm được nguồn sạc. Một cuộc gọi quan trọng, tin nhắn cần phản hồi hay chỉ đơn giản là nhu cầu sử dụng bản đồ khi đang di chuyển đều có thể trở thành vấn đề nếu thiết bị tắt nguồn.
Thực tế, Apple đã tích hợp sẵn nhiều công cụ phục vụ mục đích này trên iPhone, qua đó giúp người dùng giữ lại lượng pin cần thiết cho những tác vụ quan trọng như gọi điện, nhắn tin hoặc sử dụng bản đồ.
Chủ động chuyển iPhone sang trạng thái tiết kiệm pin
Nếu sử dụng iPhone hỗ trợ Apple Intelligence và chạy iOS 26, người dùng có thể tận dụng Adaptive Power. Tính năng này có khả năng phân tích cách sử dụng thiết bị và tự điều chỉnh một số hoạt động nhằm giảm mức tiêu thụ năng lượng.
Khi cần thiết, hệ thống có thể giảm nhẹ độ sáng màn hình, điều chỉnh hiệu năng và hạn chế một số hoạt động chạy nền. Adaptive Power cũng có thể tự kích hoạt Low Power Mode khi mức pin giảm xuống 20%.
Trên iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max và iPhone Air, tính năng này được bật sẵn. Với những thiết bị tương thích khác, người dùng có thể kiểm tra và kích hoạt trong phần Cài đặt > Pin.
Low Power Mode cũng là lựa chọn đáng cân nhắc khi pin bắt đầu xuống thấp. Thay vì chờ đến mức 20%, người dùng có thể thiết lập để chế độ này tự động kích hoạt sớm hơn thông qua ứng dụng Phím tắt.
Chẳng hạn, nếu biết mình phải ở ngoài cả ngày và không có điều kiện sạc, có thể thiết lập tự động hóa để Low Power Mode được bật khi pin còn 30% hoặc 40%. Cách này giúp dành lại phần năng lượng còn lại cho những nhu cầu quan trọng hơn.
Với các mẫu iPhone có màn hình Always-On Display, việc tắt tính năng này cũng là một phương án đơn giản. Always-On Display cho phép thời gian, widget và một số thông tin tiếp tục xuất hiện trên màn hình khóa ngay cả khi điện thoại đã khóa. Dù hệ thống có nhiều cơ chế tự động để hạn chế tiêu thụ điện, màn hình tắt hoàn toàn vẫn là lựa chọn tiết kiệm năng lượng hơn.
Người dùng có thể vào Cài đặt > Màn hình & Độ sáng để tắt Always-On Display. Trong trường hợp vẫn muốn sử dụng, việc giảm bớt nội dung hiển thị cũng có thể hạn chế phần nào mức tiêu thụ năng lượng.
Giảm những tính năng không cần thiết
Trên các mẫu iPhone trang bị ProMotion, màn hình có thể đạt tần số quét tối đa 120 Hz, mang lại cảm giác cuộn trang và chuyển động mượt mà. Tuy nhiên, khi ưu tiên thời lượng pin, người dùng có thể giới hạn tốc độ này xuống 60 Hz.
Tùy chọn nằm trong Cài đặt > Trợ năng > Chuyển động > Giới hạn tốc độ khung hình. Việc giảm tần số quét sẽ đánh đổi một phần độ mượt để đổi lấy khả năng tiết kiệm năng lượng.
Một thay đổi khác dễ thực hiện là chuyển giao diện sang Dark Mode. Với màn hình OLED, các điểm ảnh hiển thị màu tối có thể tiêu thụ ít năng lượng hơn so với những vùng sáng. Hiệu quả có thể đáng chú ý hơn khi người dùng phải duy trì độ sáng màn hình cao trong môi trường nhiều ánh sáng.
Bên cạnh màn hình, hệ thống định vị cũng là yếu tố cần kiểm tra. Nhiều ứng dụng có thể yêu cầu quyền truy cập vị trí và tiếp tục sử dụng dịch vụ định vị trong quá trình hoạt động. Nếu không thực sự cần thiết, người dùng có thể vào Cài đặt > Quyền riêng tư & Bảo mật > Dịch vụ định vị để xem lại quyền của từng ứng dụng.
Các ứng dụng bản đồ hoặc gọi xe có thể cần quyền vị trí thường xuyên, trong khi nhiều ứng dụng khác chỉ cần quyền khi đang sử dụng. Việc thu hẹp danh sách ứng dụng được phép truy cập vị trí sẽ giúp hạn chế những hoạt động nền không cần thiết.
Tương tự, Background App Refresh cho phép ứng dụng cập nhật nội dung ngay cả khi người dùng không mở chúng. Nếu cần tiết kiệm pin, có thể tắt hoàn toàn tính năng này hoặc chỉ giữ lại cho những ứng dụng thực sự cần cập nhật liên tục.
Ưu tiên pin cho những việc quan trọng
Thông báo và Live Activities cũng là những tính năng thường bị bỏ qua khi người dùng tìm cách tiết kiệm pin. Mỗi thông báo mới có thể khiến màn hình bật sáng, trong khi Live Activities liên tục cập nhật dữ liệu theo thời gian thực.
Trong trường hợp pin sắp cạn, người dùng có thể tắt thông báo của những ứng dụng không quan trọng hoặc sử dụng Scheduled Summary để gom thông báo. Các chế độ Focus cũng có thể được thiết lập nhằm hạn chế thông báo trong những khoảng thời gian nhất định.
Một chi tiết nhỏ khác là phản hồi xúc giác khi gõ bàn phím. Tính năng này tạo cảm giác chân thực khi nhập liệu nhưng sử dụng mô-tơ rung, đồng nghĩa với một phần năng lượng được tiêu thụ. Người dùng thường xuyên nhắn tin hoặc soạn thảo có thể tắt tùy chọn này trong Cài đặt > Âm thanh & Cảm ứng > Phản hồi bàn phím.
Cuối cùng, người dùng nên kiểm tra trực tiếp mục Pin trong Cài đặt để tìm ra ứng dụng đang tiêu thụ năng lượng bất thường. Trên iOS 26, hệ thống cung cấp thêm thông tin về mức sử dụng pin và các nguyên nhân như hoạt động nền hoặc thông báo.
Thay vì tắt hàng loạt tính năng, việc xác định đúng ứng dụng đang tiêu hao nhiều năng lượng sẽ giúp người dùng đưa ra lựa chọn phù hợp hơn. Một ứng dụng liên tục chạy nền hoặc gửi quá nhiều thông báo có thể là nguyên nhân khiến pin giảm nhanh mà người dùng không nhận ra.

articles.title: BenQ's first dual-monitor desk lamp will give your screens a glow up - Engadget
articles.text:
BenQ's first dual-monitor desk lamp will give your screens a glow up
I love lamp, but BenQ's most luxurious lighting comes at a steep cost.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
We spend more time with our screens than ever before these days, and few are more aware of that fact than BenQ, a brand well known among PC gamers, creatives and cinephiles. The company is launching two new monitor light bars today, the most notable of which is the ScreenBar Max, the first ScreenBar designed for dual-monitor setups. If you, like me, spend most of your workday (and a solid amount of your free time) plopped in front of computer monitors, you might know that eye strain can be a significant danger. Even if you keep your screens at a reasonable brightness and don't sit too close, the contrast between the light from the screens and the darkness of the wall behind them can still exacerbate strain, eventually causing a condition called computer vision syndrome.
One way to alleviate screen strain is to use a bias light, a lamp that shines backward onto the wall behind your screen to reduce the contrast between the two. While you're at it, you'll want a desk lamp to better see your keyboard, mouse and paper documents. The BenQ ScreenBar Max has both a bias light and desk lamp, and is large enough to stretch across two monitors while illuminating a large desk with light of a truly pristine quality. Equally as large, however, is the amount of money you'll need to cough up for it. I've spent the past several days with a review sample of this premium peripheral, and it's certainly an impressive piece of kit. The only question is whether its quality can compensate for the sticker shock of its price tag.
The BenQ ScreenBar Max is impressive, but expensive
I've been testing the ScreenBar Max for the past five days, and my preliminary impression is that this is indeed a very nice desk lamp and bias light combo, especially for multi-screen setups. It's got a price tag to match, though. The ScreenBar Max will set you back a cool $289, with another $39 if you want the optional stand. That makes this far and away the most expensive ScreenBar product from BenQ to date. You could buy four or five cheaper lamps at that price, and while they might not feel as premium, they'd offer most of the functionality.
What cheaper lamps won't match are the bells and whistles BenQ has included on the ScreenBar Max. My favorite feature is presence sensing, which uses a high frequency mmWave sensor to turn the lamp on automatically as you approach your workstation. I initially envisioned a number of ways this feature could fall on its face or become an annoyance — but to my delight, it worked quite well. My desk is next to a door, but the ScreenBar Max never activated when I walked in or out. Even pushing my chair in under the desk as I crossed the room behind it didn't cause the sensor to trigger. Only when it sensed me sitting down did the Max illuminate, pleasantly rising in luminance rather than turning on all at once.
Let there be (some truly excellent) light
The ScreenBar Max allows the brightness level of the bias light and screen lamp to be controlled independently of one another. Only the temperature level, which has a range of 2,700 to 6,000 Kelvin, is fixed across both lights. My small gripe here is that, in order to adjust one of the lights, you must toggle a a single mode selector button between bias light, desk light and both until you reach the one you want to change. It's one or two more steps than strictly necessary, and while I wouldn't knock a cheaper light bar for it, nitpicks start to feel more justified at this price point.
What I cannot nitpick is the ScreenBar Max's performance as a light bar. It's hard to translate into words, but some that sprang to mind in the course of my testing were "pristine," "precise" and "heavenly." BenQ rates the color rendering index (CRI) at Ra ≥95, Rf >96, and Rg ~100, or in plain English, studio grade. I can find no cause to doubt that claim. In my testing, there was never any harshness, flickering or heat.
In addition to the aforementioned mode selector, the ScreenBar Max has a few other handy buttons on its capacitive control panel. There's another toggle to turn the presence sensing on or off, along with brightness and temperature rockers. An auto-dim shortcut will produce an ambient brightness of 700 lux using the light sensor on top of the unit, while a monitor reading mode shortcut adjusts the temperature to 4,000 Kelvin (i.e. neutral white) before doing the same. Lastly, a favorite shortcut provides quick access to a user-determined lighting profile, and a power button does exactly what it says.
I love lamp, but it's a tough sell at this price
Installing the ScreenBar Max was easy enough. The base uses a twist-down C-clamp for easy desk installation, and a power cable can be run down the back into an outlet.
Setup won't be seamless for everyone, and my biggest issue with the ScreenBar Max ended up being a lack of adjustability. My desk has a cable management box where I would naturally want to install it, so I ended up installing it on my monitor riser instead. The light bar itself can be extended forward a fair amount, but not as far backward as you might wish if your monitors are wall mounted.
My dual monitor setup is a 27-inch IPS panel from ASUS alongside a 14.6-inch OLED tablet from Samsung, with the latter positioned off-axis for glanceable information. The ScreenBar Max did not cast glare on either screen, though it did shine off the aluminum rail of the Samsung tablet ever so slightly. It easily illuminated the entire surface of my 63-inch Eureka Gaming desk.
The ScreenBar Max earns its place in the upper echelons of monitor light bars. I've rarely felt more like Tony Stark than when it springs to life as I sit down to work, and the light it produces is pristine. It feels luxurious in a way that's hard to convey in print. But I can't say I'd spend my own hard-earned cash on the ScreenBar Max when I could get most of the same functionality at a more reasonable price. If you can get this monitor light expensed to the company card, by all means, treat yourself. But if the price tag has you on the fence, look elsewhere.

articles.title: The Supreme Court’s Mail-In Ballot Ruling Is a Step Toward Chaos in the Midterms
articles.text:
The US Supreme Court ruled on Monday that President Donald Trump’s executive order imposing severe restrictions on voting by mail ahead of November’s midterms can proceed. While a nationwide injunction preventing the US Postal Service from implementing the order remains in place, election officials and experts believe Monday’s ruling could still result in chaos and voters being disenfranchised.
The Supreme Court ruling, which split along ideological lines, paused an injunction by a federal judge in Boston that prevented the Trump administration from applying provisions of the executive order to 23 states, along with the District of Columbia.
The court didn’t rule on the legality of the order, which seeks to impose federal oversight on elections that are, under the Constitution, controlled by states. The conservative majority ruled, rather, that the states that brought the lawsuit did not have standing because they could not show actual damage caused by the order.
“The court’s disposition of this application does not mean that any measure taken by the government to implement the order will necessarily be lawful,” the majority wrote in an unsigned opinion. “On that score, time will tell.”
The executive order is predicated on the baseless allegations pushed by Trump and his allies that widespread mail-in voter fraud has altered the outcomes of recent elections. (To put the claims in perspective, a database of supposed voter fraud incidents, maintained by the right-wing Heritage Foundation and dating back to 1980, contains fewer than 100 proven examples of noncitizen voting of any sort.) Experts and election officials have long warned that if implemented in full, the executive order would disenfranchise millions of voters. In a blistering dissent, Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson agreed, writing that the ruling could create a “Kafkaesque nightmare [that] needlessly injects chaos and uncertainty into the upcoming midterm elections.”
Despite the possibly temporary nature of this victory, election denial groups cheered the result as a major victory for so-called election integrity efforts. And experts worry that even if Trump’s executive order is eventually blocked, the decision will still have a direct impact on voter turnout in November by sowing doubts about the legitimacy of mail-in voting.
“Voting rights organizations have experienced first-hand the significant confusion that President Trump’s executive order is causing right now,” the counsel and plaintiffs in a second lawsuit against Trump’s executive order wrote in a statement on Monday. “With the November election right around the corner, nonpartisan voting rights groups should be fully engaged in the vital work of educating all eligible voters to prepare to cast their ballots. Instead, plaintiffs and similar organizations are scrambling to understand how the rules may change while fielding inquiries from voters who rely on mail ballots and who are confused and fearful about how they will exercise their right to vote.”
The Executive Order
Almost one third of US voters cast their ballots by mail, including around one in four Republican voters. (Trump himself voted by mail in this year’s GOP primary in Florida.) In eight states, more than 70 percent of ballots were cast by mail during the 2024 elections.
Despite years of false claims from Trump and his allies about widespread mail-in voter fraud, there is no evidence to back up those claims. But in March, Trump signed an executive order titled “Ensuring Citizenship Verification and Integrity in Federal Elections.” The order contains three distinct provisions.
The first directs the Department of Homeland Security to compile a “State Citizenship List” of individuals confirmed to be US citizens and deemed eligible to vote in each state. The list would be compiled from Social Security Administration records, Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) data, and federal citizenship and naturalization records. The list would need to be sent to states 60 days before the election. That date is Friday, September 4—just 11 days after the Supreme Court ruling.
“This would create a parallel federal eligibility infrastructure on top of existing state voter rolls,” Issue One, a nonprofit seeking to reduce the role of money in politics, wrote shortly after the order was issued.
The second provision targets election officials by demanding that the US attorney general “prioritize the investigation and, as appropriate, the prosecution of State and local officials … who issue Federal ballots to individuals not eligible to vote in a Federal election.”
The final provision in the order directs the USPS to create new rules for absentee and mail-in ballots. Under the rules, states would need to provide the USPS with a list of voters they intend to send ballots to. The order prevents the USPS from sending ballots to anyone not on the list. This rule would require the printing of millions of new ballot envelopes with trackable barcodes.
Last week, before the Supreme Court ruling was issued, the USPS issued a 95-page final rule explaining how it plans to enforce Trump’s proposed changes to mail-in voting in order to “reduce the risk of fraud, and help protect the integrity of federal elections.” The rule compares mail-in ballots to fake bombs or cremated animal remains. The New York Times reported on Monday that Trump is seeking to take control over the USPS board by stacking it with members who have questioned the outcome of the 2020 election.
The provisions of the executive order were mostly blocked by federal courts before the Trump administration appealed the rulings to the Supreme Court in July. Earlier this month, the administration pushed the court to issue a ruling quickly, claiming that failing to do so would cause “irreparable harm to the federal government, the public, and election integrity.”
While the states are likely to file another lawsuit once the USPS rule goes into effect on Wednesday, the Supreme Court decision will still likely cause disruption, given how close the general election is.
“The Court seemed to create complete chaos leading up to the midterm elections, waiting weeks after an administration filing, and just days before mail ballots go out, to completely rewrite the rules of the election,” David Becker, the head of the Center for Election Innovation and Research and a former Justice Department lawyer, wrote in an emailed statement.
That chaos will hit election officials the hardest.
“From a strictly practical perspective, there simply is just not enough time to implement the proposed requirements for the 2026 general election,” Stuart Holmes, director of elections in Washington state, tells WIRED.
Holmes said that county election offices already have ballot packet mailing materials printed and ready to mail, and that destroying and reprinting them is not realistic, financially or otherwise. The USPS rules would also require new envelope designs, which would in turn need to be reviewed and approved by the USPS to ensure compliance with their automation equipment.
“Even if new designs could be developed and approved in time, it is unrealistic to expect the limited number of printing vendors serving Washington’s counties to produce entirely new supplies of ballot envelopes for every county before the general election without significant disruption,” Holmes adds.
Finally, Holmes flagged that the demands of maintaining the USPS lists required under the order would be virtually impossible. “Voter registration data does not remain static. Voters continually update their registrations, ineligible voters are removed from the rolls, and newly eligible voters are added,” he says. “Meeting the proposed reporting requirements would require the Office of the Secretary of State to dedicate staff to provide updated information to USPS while those same staff are already responsible for other essential list maintenance and election preparation activities.”
