articles.title: The Nokia 300 Charge doubles as a 10W powerbank - Engadget
articles.text:
The Nokia 300 Charge doubles as a 10W powerbank
How many smartphones can boast that?
For a long time, dumb phones were positioned as an alternative to smartphones and their app abundance. But Nokia is making it very clear that its new 300 Charge can actually be your other phone's best friend, as the device also doubles as a portable powerbank.
At first glance, the 300 Charge looks like any old-fashioned Nokia dumb phone, but pretty quickly you'll notice that there's a bit more chunk on show here. That's because the phone houses a 3,700mAh battery that promises to deliver up to 37 hours of talk time and 40 hours of standby.
The really interesting part, though, is "powerbank mode," which activates 10W reverse-wired charging via the included 4-in-1 cable. Adapters for Micro USB, USB-C and USB-A are included. The 300 Charge probably doesn't have the juice to be your main powerbank if you travel with a lot of gear, but it should be useful in a pinch.
Adding to its good-gadget-to-have-around vibe is the high-power built-in LED flashlight, which Nokia says is up to 4x brighter than the one in the Nokia 105. Another reason to find room for it in your bag.
Nokia describes the 300 Charge as both "rugged" and "sleek," and only the second of those terms is contentious, thanks to the textured grip around the back and sides, which should make the phone both tough and easy to grip onto.
Otherwise, the 300 Charge is a very basic phone. It employs a Unisoc SC6531E chipset and has 4GB of both RAM and internal storage. The QVGA camera will not take impressive photos, and you aren't going to be doing a lot on the 2.4-inch display. Still, there is a 3.5mm jack, which is more than you can say for a lot of far more expensive phones on the market.
There's currently no word on a US release, but expect a sub-$50 price tag if it does arrive at some point in the future.

articles.title: Dùng Chrome suốt 14 năm cứ tưởng là nhất, ai ngờ chuyển sang trình duyệt này mới thấy tốt hơn bao nhiêu
articles.text:
Trình duyệt của Google ngày càng giật lag, chậm chạp mỗi khi mở nhiều tab cùng lúc. Hóa ra việc chuyển sang một trình duyệt khác lại không phức tạp đến thế.
Không ít người đã trung thành với Google Chrome trong nhiều năm qua. Nhưng cũng khá nhiều trong số đó đã từ bỏ trình duyệt này để đến với lựa chọn phù hợp hơn.
Cây bút Rahul Naskar từ Android Police đã chính thức nói lời chia tay với Google Chrome để chuyển sang dùng Microsoft Edge trên chiếc laptop của mình sau khi mọi giới hạn chịu đựng bị phá vỡ.
Trình duyệt của Google bắt đầu xuất hiện tình trạng giật lag, chậm chạp mỗi khi mở nhiều tab cùng lúc. Ngay cả khi đã nâng cấp cấu hình máy tính lẫn can thiệp vào các cài đặt ẩn, tình trạng nghẽn hiệu năng vẫn nhất quyết không chịu biến mất.
Không chỉ giải quyết dứt điểm nỗi đau đầu trên máy tính, Edge còn mang lại trải nghiệm duyệt web trên di động tốt đến không ngờ.
Dưới đây là lý do mà cây bút này quyết dứt hẳn với Google Chrome.
Bước ngoặt thay đổi cuộc chơi
Ban đầu, tôi đã cố bám trụ với Chrome lâu nhất có thể. Tôi vẫn nhớ như in lần đầu tiên trải nghiệm nó trên chiếc điện thoại Android đầu đời cách đây 14 năm.
Tôi từng hoàn toàn hài lòng với những gì Chrome mang lại, và qua năm tháng, nó dần trở thành một phần gần như không thể thay thế. Thế nhưng, chỉ cần một sự cố hiệu năng nghiêm trọng là đủ để buộc tôi phải tìm kiếm một phương án dự phòng.
Dù kế hoạch ban đầu chỉ là dùng thử Edge trên chiếc laptop Windows, tôi rốt cuộc lại đưa nó lên toàn bộ các thiết bị Android của mình.
Tôi đổ phần lớn trách nhiệm cho việc tối ưu hóa kém cỏi trên hệ điều hành Windows, điều mà Google đã không dành đủ tâm sức để khắc phục suốt nhiều năm qua.
Là một người dùng lâu năm và trung thành, tôi đã chạm tới giới hạn cuối cùng.
Dù đã chuẩn bị tâm lý cho việc sẽ thiếu hụt một vài tính năng quen thuộc, Edge lại khiến tôi hoàn toàn bất ngờ bởi bộ công cụ mạnh mẽ cùng khả năng tùy biến linh hoạt mà nó mang lại.
Cài đặt trọn vẹn các tiện ích mở rộng yêu thích như trên máy tính
Đối với những tín đồ của Chrome, việc rời bỏ hệ sinh thái Google thường đồng nghĩa với việc chấp nhận đánh đổi. Băn khoăn lớn nhất của tôi là phải bỏ lại thư viện các tiện ích mở rộng (extension) và plug-in trên máy tính mà mình vẫn dùng hằng ngày.
Thật nhẹ nhõm khi Edge lại sở hữu một ưu thế vượt trội so với Chrome trên hệ điều hành Android: hỗ trợ cài đặt các tiện ích mở rộng di động một cách chính thức.
Tôi đã quá mệt mỏi với việc ứng dụng YouTube liên tục ép người dùng xem Shorts, trong khi app gốc trên di động lại chẳng có lấy một công tắc đơn giản nào để ẩn chúng khỏi giao diện.
Chuyển sang Edge, tôi xem YouTube trực tiếp trên trình duyệt và cài thêm tiện ích Unhook. Extension này giúp dọn sạch toàn bộ các video Shorts, đồng thời loại bỏ luôn cả những nguồn cấp dữ liệu phiền phức như mục đề xuất hay phần bình luận.
Sở hữu bộ công cụ hữu ích chuẩn máy tính ngay trên màn hình smartphone là một trải nghiệm vô cùng đắt giá. Nó giúp tôi không còn phải mò mẫm bật laptop mỗi khi cần kiểm tra lịch sử biến động giá cả.
Chưa dừng lại ở đó, Edge còn tích hợp sẵn một trợ lý mua sắm thông minh, tự động cảnh báo các ưu đãi mới cũng như các đợt giảm giá mà không cần phải cài đặt thêm bất kỳ plug-in nào.
Đây chỉ là vài ví dụ tiêu biểu trong thiết lập hằng ngày của tôi. Ngoài ra, tôi còn vận hành mượt mà các ứng dụng quản lý mật khẩu của bên thứ ba cùng các tiện ích bổ sung cho Google Keep.
Trải nghiệm tuyệt vời với các tiện ích mở rộng trên Edge đã đập tan hoàn toàn mối lo về việc sẽ bỏ lỡ những tính năng quan trọng từ Chrome.
Không còn bị lệ thuộc vào sự kiểm soát của Google
Edge vốn không phải là một trình duyệt thuần về bảo mật quyền riêng tư. Tuy nhiên, tôi vẫn ưu tiên lựa chọn nó thay vì Chrome mỗi khi muốn né tránh việc bị Google thu thập dữ liệu quá đà.
Sử dụng tài khoản Microsoft đồng nghĩa với việc Google sẽ thu thập được ít điểm dữ liệu hơn để phục vụ cho cỗ máy quảng cáo của họ.
Dù Microsoft vẫn thu thập dữ liệu cá nhân, Edge lại cung cấp cho người dùng khả năng kiểm soát rất chi tiết để hạn chế hành vi theo dõi đó.
Các công cụ chặn theo dõi tích hợp sẵn mang lại sự linh hoạt cao. Chế độ Cân bằng (Balanced) mặc định sẽ tự động chặn các trình theo dõi của bên thứ ba từ các trang web bạn chưa từng ghé thăm, đồng thời hạn chế các nội dung và quảng cáo mang tính cá nhân hóa.
Khi chuyển sang chế độ Nghiêm ngặt (Strict), trình duyệt sẽ chặn đại đa số các trình theo dõi trên mọi website, loại bỏ quảng cáo hướng mục tiêu triệt để hơn nhiều so với chế độ Cân bằng.
Đặc biệt hơn, Edge tích hợp sẵn một trình chặn quảng cáo trên di động với hiệu quả tương đương các extension trên máy tính. Điều này giúp tôi không còn phải cài đặt thêm ứng dụng chặn quảng cáo của bên thứ ba hay phải chuyển sang một trình duyệt nào khác.
Tối ưu hiệu năng và vận hành mượt mà hơn
Edge đã chứng minh độ tin cậy đáng kinh ngạc khi xử lý mượt mà hàng chục tab cùng một lúc.
Dù Chrome chưa từng hoạt động quá tệ trên điện thoại của tôi, Edge vẫn mang lại cảm giác phản hồi nhanh hơn rõ rệt và tiết kiệm tài nguyên tốt hơn khi phải gánh các hệ thống quản trị nội dung (CMS) nặng nề trên phần cứng Android — bao gồm cả chiếc Galaxy Tab S10 FE khi bật Chế độ máy tính (Desktop Mode).
Tôi có thể duy trì hàng loạt tab hoạt động và chuyển đổi qua lại giữa các tác vụ một cách trơn tru, dù chiếc máy tính bảng chỉ sở hữu 8GB RAM. Nó cũng hạn chế tối đa tình trạng quá nhiệt gây giảm hiệu năng cũng như hiện tượng hao pin bất thường trong các phiên duyệt web nặng.
Thỉnh thoảng, vài sự cố nhỏ vẫn xuất hiện rải rác, nhưng hiện tượng giật lag hiệu năng là vô cùng hiếm gặp trên các thiết bị di động của tôi, và đặc biệt là trên PC.
Dù sao đi nữa, Edge mang lại cho tôi sự tin tưởng tuyệt đối khi sử dụng, và đó chính là bước ngoặt quyết định.
Tự do tùy biến Edge theo phong cách cá nhân
Không chỉ dừng lại ở khả năng tối ưu hóa tốt hơn và kiểm soát quyền riêng tư chặt chẽ, Microsoft Edge còn sở hữu nhiều tiện ích thông minh cùng khả năng cá nhân hóa sâu rộng.
Tính năng Drop tích hợp sẵn cho phép truyền tệp, hình ảnh và đường link giữa các thiết bị cực kỳ nhanh chóng mà không cần phải lục tìm lại lịch sử duyệt web hay truy cập vào các ứng dụng lưu trữ đám mây.
Dù tôi vẫn có thể thực hiện thao tác tương tự thông qua Google Drive, việc tính năng này được tích hợp trực tiếp vào trình duyệt giúp trải nghiệm chia sẻ dữ liệu trở nên nhanh gọn và tiện lợi hơn rất nhiều.
Là một người thích mày mò tùy chỉnh giao diện trên Pixel hay Galaxy, tôi cực kỳ đánh giá cao mức độ can thiệp giao diện ngay bên trong trình duyệt web này.
Tôi có thể áp dụng các chủ đề (theme) tùy chỉnh từ thư viện của Microsoft hoặc tự phối màu theo sở thích.
Rất khó để quay trở lại với Chrome
Sau 14 năm gắn bó khăng khít với Chrome, việc bước ra khỏi hệ sinh thái của Google tất nhiên khiến tôi tốn một khoảng thời gian ngắn để thích nghi.
Là một người dùng Chrome lâu năm, tôi đôi lúc vẫn nhớ sự đồng bộ liền mạch với các ứng dụng trong hệ sinh thái Google. Tôi cũng phải tự tay chuyển thủ công một số mật khẩu và tài khoản không thể tự động đồng bộ sang Edge.
Tuy nhiên, đó chỉ là những phiền thoái nhỏ nếu so với những lợi ích lớn hơn: một trải nghiệm duyệt web ổn định và khả năng hạn chế bị Google thu thập dữ liệu cá nhân.
Rời bỏ hệ sinh thái của Google đã giúp tôi nhận ra rằng mình không nhất thiết phải tự trói buộc bản thân vào đó.
Nếu Chrome vẫn duy trì khả năng tối ưu tốt trên laptop lẫn điện thoại và chịu khó bỏ chút công sức để khắc phục các sự cố, có lẽ tôi vẫn sẽ tiếp tục là một người dùng trung thành của họ.

articles.title: Claude Cowork finally remembers what you told the app in chat | TechCrunch
articles.text:
A change to Claude’s memory system will eliminate one of the most annoying things about using agents — the constant need to rebrief the AI on things it already knows. On Tuesday, Anthropic announced it’s merging the memory system used by chat and Claude Cowork, which means that Claude will always remember what it learned in one area, even when you’re engaging with it in another.
Anthropic is also exposing what Claude has retained in its memory, allowing users to read, edit, or delete information on any topic.
The update will improve the experience for Claude’s users as it will allow them to more seamlessly move between the research phase and taking action.
Before, you may have developed ideas for projects over time while chatting with Claude, but when it came time to actually enact the changes, you’d have to start over by telling Cowork all the details. This was incredibly frustrating. The update makes Claude now feel like one continuous assistant, rather than two separate products under one roof.
Anthropic offers an example of someone needing to draft an update for their manager or an agenda for a conference, where Cowork would already understand the references because of the past conversations about the matter at hand. For instance, it would know the headcount, city, and speakers at the conference, so you wouldn’t have to re-input that information.
In addition, Claude will now add topics to its memory as you chat, instead of summarizing a conversation when it ends. That makes it easier to move back and forth between chat and Cowork, as the new memories are more quickly updated and shared between the two experiences, even if the chat is ongoing.
Anthropic says that, by default, Claude won’t store personal or sensitive information like your health data, race, ethnicity, religious beliefs, politics, gender identity, and more. However, users can opt to enable these things by toggling on “include sensitive topics in memory” if they prefer. The app will also notify users whenever a sensitive topic is saved in memory.
However, the company says that Claude won’t ever save certain things, like government-issued ID and Social Security numbers, criminal history, immigration status, or other things that violate its acceptable use policy.
The memory feature is enabled by default on Free, Pro, and Max plans across web, desktop, and mobile. On iOS and Android, users will need to update their app to the latest version.

articles.title: Apple Refreshes the Mac Mini and Mac Studio, Both With New AI-Ready Chips
articles.text:
Apple has announced fresh versions of the Mac Mini and Mac Studio desktop computers, alongside some new chips: the M6 and M5 Ultra.
Neither Mac desktop has undergone any physical changes on the exterior, but the long-awaited update brings these Macs back into stock after being difficult to buy for most of this year. Importantly, this serves as our first introduction to the M6 chip, which we will likely see much more of in future MacBooks.
Skipping the M5 entirely, the Mac Mini now comes in two flavors: the M6 and the M5 Pro. The M5 Pro is the same chip that's currently found in the MacBook Pro, but the M6 is brand new. It's the first Apple Silicon part to be built on 2-nanometer process technology and also adds extra cores to the mix. This is a 12-core CPU—another first for Apple—broken down into two super cores, four performances cores, and six efficiency cores.
New here are the performance cores, which Apple says are designed to speed up multithreaded tasks while preserving efficiency. Apple claims the M6 is 20 percent faster than the M5 in multithreaded performance and 40 percent faster than the M4.
The M6 comes with a faster GPU too, adding two more cores to the mix for a total of 12 GPU cores. This is also the first Mac Mini to have Neural Accelerators for faster on-device AI performance, a feature that launched in the M5 chip last year. The result is a Mac Mini that Apple claims is twice as fast as the M4 Mac Mini, along with providing higher throughput for gaming. Lastly, the M6 Mac mini also comes with what Apple calls a “dual 16-core Neural Engine," which doubles the peak AI performance.
In addition to the extra performance, however, it also comes with a $200 price increase. The M6 Mac Mini now starts at $899 for the model with 16 GB of unified memory. The Mac Mini can still be configured with up to 32 GB of unified memory, and Apple says the tiny desktop is 40 percent faster, with bandwidth now up to 170 GB per second.
The M5 Ultra Arrives
The Mac Studio is also receiving a significant update. Like the Mac Mini, it still comes in two flavors: the M5 Max and the new M5 Ultra. This is the fourth generation of the Mac Studio to come out, with the M3 Ultra (and M3 Max) model coming out in early 2025.
Apple proudly claims that the M5 Ultra is Apple's most powerful chip ever, and the first to use a “quad-die” architecture. Apple's “Ultra” chips have always connected two Max dies together using using a technology called UltraFusion across a high-speed interconnect. The difference this time is that the M5 Max already had two dies itself, which is where the four dies come from. To keep those four chips running as fast as possible, the next version of UltraFusion increases the inter-die bandwidth to over 4.4 TB per second, allowing the whole array to function as a single CPU.
M5 Ultra Mac Studio comes with four more CPU cores for a total of 36. There are still 80 GPU cores (the same as on the M3 Ultra), but the M5-specific improvements to the GPU apply here for better overall performance.
In a briefing on the Mac Studio, Apple even discussed the ability to connect multiple Mac Studios together over Thunderbolt 5 to run frontier-level LLMs with over a trillion parameters locally, allowing the four systems to share memory. Hypothetically, that allows you to run models locally on a Mac that just weren't possible before. Apparently, four Mac Studios can even be connected in this way to run over a standard wall outlet.
Both the Mac Mini and Mac Studio are available for preorder starting today and will come with macOS 27 Golden Gate preinstalled. However, systems won't ship until September 22. In a briefing, Apple said this delay wouldn't be reflective of shipping times for these new Mac Mini or Mac Studio systems.

articles.title: Claude's memory now works across both chats and Cowork sessions - Engadget
articles.text:
Claude's memory now works across both chats and Cowork sessions
Plus, Anthropic is giving users more control over what memories Claude saves.
Since last summer, Claude has had the ability to remember past conversations, but often those "memories" have been fragmented. Sometimes by design, and at other times due to limitations in Claude's architecture. That's partly changing today, with Anthropic releasing a major update to its memory feature set.
The company's models can now access and carry over memories across both Claude the chatbot and Claude Cowork. Cowork, if you need a reminder, is the computer use agent Anthropic released at the start of the year. You can use it to automate rote tasks you repeat often through the day. "When Cowork runs a task in the cloud, what Claude remembers from your chats is there, and vice versa," says Anthropic. In practice, this means you'll need to repeat yourself less often when using Cowork since Claude will have access to context from your chats. Today's update is well-timed since it builds on a recent upgrade Anthropic released for its Claude for Chrome browser extension where it made Cowork available through the plugin. Since that change, conversations you have in the Chrome side panel now become part of your usage history.
Anthropic is also giving users more control over Claude's memory. Over the last few weeks, users have been able to see the chatbot's memories organized by topic, and edit the specifics of each topic from Claude's settings menu. To that the company is adding a new "include sensitive topics in memory" option. "By default, Claude does not store topics related to personal or sensitive subject matter, like your health, race, ethnicity, religious beliefs, politics, gender identity, and other similar areas," explains Anthropic.
If you flip on the sensitive topics toggle, Claude will begin adding those topics to its memory. Each time it does so, you will see a notification. Anthropic notes Claude won't retroactively add past conversations to its memory, and that you can turn off the feature at any time, as well as edit and delete what it saves. As for why it's making this change now, the company reasons "what some consider sensitive, others may consider useful for Claude to remember." Anthropic notes Claude will not save certain information, including your social security number, criminal history, immigration status, even if you have the sensitive topics toggle enabled.
Memory is available (and enabled by default) for all Free, Pro and Max accounts. On mobile, update to the latest version of the Claude Android or iOS app to see the new updates.

articles.title: Waymo robotaxis are headed to Munich | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Waymo said Tuesday it plans to launch a robotaxi service in Munich, months after the Alphabet-owned autonomous vehicle company set up an entity in Germany.
The company still must weave its way through mapping and testing, as well as clear regulatory hurdles before it can launch commercial operations.
Waymo will begin, as it has in the other 11 cities where it has commercial robotaxi operations, by first manually driving its vehicles to map the streets of Munich. It will then test its autonomous vehicles with human safety drivers behind the wheel, before removing them. Waymo typically allows its employees, media, and other invited guests to ride in its driverless vehicles at this stage.
The company will eventually open its robotaxis to limited service, and eventually to all riders once it receives the regulatory approval required to operate commercially. Waymo said in a blog post on Tuesday that it is working with Germany’s Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA), state authorities, and local officials, and expects to open commercial ride-hailing to the public toward the end of 2027.
Waymo’s entry into Germany comes more than five years after the country’s lawmakers adopted legislation to allow driverless vehicles on public roads, and in that process making it the first country in the European Union to create a legal framework for Level 4 autonomous driving. Level 4 autonomy is a designation by the Society of Automobile Engineers (SAE) that means the self-driving system handles all the driving, with no expectation of a human taking over, in certain conditions or environments.
This legal framework has made Germany a hotspot for autonomous vehicle testing. Today, several companies, including Mobileye and Volkswagen, hold permits to test their autonomous vehicles in the country, according to the KBA’s latest data. Waymo does not currently have any permits.
However, the vast majority, including U.K. self-driving startup Wayve, and Israel-based Autobrains, hold Level 3 permits. Level 3, or conditional automated driving, is a system that can handle all the driving within specific operating conditions, such as low speeds on highways, but the driver must be able to take over when needed.
Germany isn’t the only overseas hotspot for AV developers. The U.K., especially London, is shaping up as another robotaxi battleground. Waymo has said it plans to launch a commercial service in London in 2026, which will pit it against Wayve and its partner Uber. Chinese tech giant Baidu has also started testing autonomous vehicles in the city as part of its partnership with Lyft and Freenow.

articles.title: Cổ phiếu Samsung lao dốc, nhà đầu tư thất vọng
articles.text:
Đầu phiên giao dịch ngày 24/8, giá cổ phiếu Samsung Electronics giảm 8% sau khi kế hoạch hoàn lợi nhuận cổ đông kỷ lục trị giá 79 tỷ USD của tập đoàn này không đáp ứng kỳ vọng của nhà đầu tư.
Hôm 21/8, nhà sản xuất chip Hàn Quốc cho biết tổng mức hoàn vốn cho cổ đông trong năm nay sẽ đạt 90.000 - 110.000 tỷ won (65 - 80 tỷ USD), trong đó có 30.000 tỷ won cổ tức bằng tiền mặt trong quý 3.
Dù con số này cao gấp 5 lần mức kỷ lục được ghi nhận vào năm 2020, các chuyên gia phân tích cho rằng vẫn thấp hơn kỳ vọng. Nhà đầu tư cũng muốn Samsung công bố chi tiết hơn về kế hoạch mua lại cổ phiếu.
Samsung cho biết vẫn duy trì chính sách phân bổ 50% dòng tiền tự do tích lũy trong giai đoạn ba năm để hoàn vốn cho cổ đông giai đoạn 2024-2026.
Trong khi đó, đối thủ SK Hynix cho biết tuần trước sẽ mua lại và hủy 40.000 tỷ won cổ phiếu quỹ. Doanh nghiệp này cũng dự kiến phân bổ hơn 50% dòng tiền tự do tạo ra trong giai đoạn 2025 - 2027 để tăng lợi ích cho cổ đông.
Trái ngược với Samsung, cổ phiếu SK Hynix tăng 0,4% trong phiên 24/8. Chỉ số KOSPI giảm 1,5%.
“Không giống SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics không đề cập khả năng nâng tỷ lệ hoàn vốn hiện tại, cũng không công bố kế hoạch hủy cổ phiếu quỹ - biện pháp có thể tác động trực tiếp hơn đến giá cổ phiếu. Đây là điều đáng thất vọng”, chuyên gia phân tích Sohn In-joon tại Eugene Securities nhận định.
Morgan Stanley đánh giá kế hoạch của Samsung là “mức hoàn vốn lớn nhưng thấp hơn đôi chút so với kỳ vọng”.
Theo Morgan Stanley, nhà đầu tư sẽ cần theo dõi quyết định của Samsung vào tháng 1 tới về việc phân bổ 60.000 - 80.000 tỷ won còn lại. Thị trường cũng chờ đợi khung chính sách hoàn vốn mới của tập đoàn, dự kiến có hiệu lực từ năm sau.
Theo Reuters

articles.title: Waymo is expanding to Germany, with service in Munich planned for 2027 - Engadget
articles.text:
Waymo is expanding to Germany, with service in Munich planned for 2027
The company has set up subsidiaries in several European countries this summer.
Waymo is quickly expanding to more territories and Germany is next on the list. The company is bringing its vehicles to Munich and it aims to start commercial service in the city — its first location in the European Union — by the end of 2027.
It will start deploying its robotaxis in the city, which is the third-largest in Germany, in the coming weeks to map local streets and begin testing with safety drivers behind the wheel. Waymo said it's working with local, state and federal officials to obtain the permits it needs to offer fully autonomous rides in Munich next year.
This is the second European country that Waymo is moving into. The company aims to start offering rides to the public in London as soon as next month. It's not stopping there, though. Waymo has established subsidiaries in several European nations in recent months, including France, Spain and the Netherlands. Those were all set up in June, around the same time as its German office. Waymo also confirmed to Zag Daily this month that it has registered a subsidiary in Switzerland.

articles.title: Life360 expands pet tracking with new $8 scannable tags and zoomie alerts | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Family location-sharing and safety app Life360 is expanding its pet-tracking capabilities on Tuesday with the launch of a new product line of $7.99 scannable pet tags and other pet-care features that tap into its tracking network technology.
Life360 expanded into pet tech last year with the launch of GPS pet trackers that leverage the lost-item-finding capabilities that the company integrated into its platform after its 2021 acquisition of AirTag rival Tile. With Tile, the company now offers not just location-sharing features for families, but also the ability for members to track other things of importance — like keys, handbags, luggage, and pets.
Since then, families on the service have added more than 8 million pets to their accounts, the company says.
However, the team found that not everyone wants to attach a bulky tracker to their pet’s collar, and not everyone needs access to location-tracking features or other advanced options like geofences and escape alerts.
In many cases, pet owners just want to put their contact information on a pet’s tag, which is what the new scannable pet tags support.
But there’s a twist. Instead of just providing a pet owner’s phone number when someone scans the QR code printed on the new pet tags, the scan also alerts the family through the Life360 app installed on the family’s smartphones. (The person who found the pet does not need to have the app for this to work.)
This helps in multiple ways — not only does it provide peace of mind to families searching for a lost pet, but it also provides the pet’s location details. That can be useful if the lost pet escapes from the finder’s control and runs off again, as the family will at least have the last known location recorded.
Families can update their contact details through the Life360 pet profile in the app.
In addition, the company is rolling out several new pet-care features for families, including tools that let families schedule “care logs” to manage and track whether the pet has been fed, walked, given medication, or had its litter cleaned. Everyone in the family can see these care routines, so they will know if the pet needs their attention.
Another fun feature is “Zoomies Alerts” for GPS trackers, which track the bursts of energy a pet has at particular points during the day or evening. A new Weekly Roundup will recap other routines, like the distance walked or information about who in the family provided the pet with the most care during the week.
With the new features, the company is also making its pet trackers more affordable. Before, the Pet GPS trackers were only available with the higher-tier Platinum and Gold subscriptions, but now they’re included with the $99-per-year Silver bundles, too.
The new pet tags and GPS trackers are sold on both the company’s website and Amazon in the U.S., Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and the U.K.

articles.title: I Road-Tripped With 12 Car Phone Mounts This Summer. This One Wins
articles.text:
A car phone mount is no longer an option—it's a necessity. Nearly every US state restricts cell phone use while driving (we see you, Montana!), and most require full hands-free operation. The best car phone mounts offer an easy view of your phone's screen without blocking your view of the road, hold your phone securely, and keep vibration to a minimum.
I've spent weeks and hundreds of miles testing car phone holders for iPhones and Android alike, on busy freeways and on potholed city roads. What I found is that the best car phone mounts aren't necessarily expensive or name brands: They're just smartly designed.
The best car phone mount for an iPhone is almost always a secure MagSafe mount. The one I keep in my car when I'm not testing other mounts is a sturdy, compact Andery suction mount ($36) that holds preternaturally fast to both my phone and dash but can also be mounted to a window. My favorite mechanical car phone holder for Android phones is a sturdy, versatile, ball-joint mount from Andobil ($30) that affixes tightly to a car's dash, windshield, or air vents.
Here are the best car phone mounts for each car and phone type. See also WIRED's guides to the Best USB Car Chargers, Best Portable Jump Starters, Best iPhone Cases and Accessories, Best MagSafe Accessories, and Best Wireless Phone Chargers.
Best Car Phone Mount for iPhones and Qi2 Phones
The world is full of bulky phone mounts that block your view of the road, inflexible phone mounts that only allow for horizontal or vertical mounting, weak suction cups, and kinda mid MagSafe attachments. And then there's this innovatively designed, wonderfully compact dash and window mount from Andery.
On flat surfaces, the nano-gel suction cup holds fast like Hodor at the door. The 22-magnet MagSafe ring allows airflow to avoid overheating, but it also holds stronger than most comparable Qi2 magnets. And unlike bulky plastic mounts, the Andery's aluminum-arm, stainless steel ring keeps a low profile and interferes minimally with one's line of sight. In fact, when affixed to my dash, this device doesn't block my view of the road at all. The ring rotates 360 degrees. The two-joint arm can either fold tightly to the mount or extend outward. No other mount I've tested combines all of these virtues.
But note you'll need a relatively flat surface to get a good bond with the suction cup. I've also seen some reports that the suction cup can lose adhesion over time if repeatedly re-mounted (and it's cussedly difficult to remove in the first place, though it leaves no residue when you do). Non-Qi2-compatible Android phones will need a MagSafe case to be compatible with this car phone holder. But if your phone has a magnet or a magnetic case, this is the simplest and most effective car phone mount I know, and it performs leagues better than other similarly designed car mounts like this one from Acer.
Note also that Andery offers a Qi2-compatible phone charger version at the expense of airflow. I haven't tested this variant yet.
Best Universal Car Phone Mount
Mechanical mounts like this one from Andobil—with holders that can be slid in sideways to securely grip the phone—are flexible for a broad range of phones and don't require MagSafe technology. But they're also mostly bulky, making them a less preferred option as a windshield or dashboard mount because this will block your field of vision.
Among all similar devices I've tested, this one from newer Chinese company Andobil is the most compact I've tested when not in use, while still offering a lot of flexibility. The nanogel suction cup on its dash mount is one of the most stable I've tested (almost aggressively stuck on, to be honest). And the extendable arm, while plastic, feels less cheap and breakable than other models. The kit also comes with an air vent mount, whose three-point design makes it among the most stable vent mounts I've tested and allows you to maneuver the phone so it does not block the vent.
This mechanical car phone holder is hard to call aesthetic. It's essentially a pad with a gripper on the side. But the grips extend to accommodate even larger phones and are able to keep the phone in place even during vigorous shaking. (If you're wondering whether I place phones in these phone mounts, and then come at them like they're a shake weight? I do.) The release button's a little awkwardly placed, and Andobil's marketing about “military standards” is a little silly on a low-cost device made with thermoplastics. But after I watched other suction cups wilt in summer heat, this Andobil's still going strong.
★ A Great, Low-Cost Air Vent Mount: If you're mounting only to your air vent, the Vanva air vent phone mount ($13) is among the cheapest mounts of any kind that I've tested, while ranking among the most secure mechanical mounts. (Actually, I like the mechanical phone holder a bit better than Andobil's.) The lockable clamp affixes easily and securely to most vertical or horizontal-slatted vents—and unlike hook-based vent mounts, it's easy to install and remove. The multi-joint ball arm can be maneuvered so you don't lose airflow from the vent, and the adjustable grips that lock in your phone can be released with a simple button press. This Vanva is a relatively flimsy plastic device, so I don't rule out that it might break someday. But its inexpensive replacement cost makes this an acceptable risk.
Best Car Phone Mount With Charger
Look, I'll be honest: I have mixed feelings about chargers on car phone mounts. The mount will have to be plugged into a car charger anyway—and at that point, I might as well just plug in the phone directly, which will usually lead to faster charging.
But convenience is in the eye of the beholder, and many people prefer to just leave the car mount plugged permanently into a car charger so they never have to worry about their phone draining while navigating on a mapping app. For y'all, here's the car mount from ESR, which offers decently fast 15-watt charging and a cooling fan to mitigate phone overheating.
The suction was effective when attached to both my window and dash, and the device is compact enough to not much hinder my field of view. Charging speed is merely moderate, enough to charge an older iPhone in a couple of hours. ESR also offers a faster-charging Qi2.2 device for twice the money, though I have not tested it.
★ A Good, Stylish Vent Charging Mount: Most vent chargers plant themselves directly into the airflow of your vent. But not all of them do. WIRED editor Julian Chokkattu recommends the Peak Design Car Vent Mount ($100). The mount stays secure on the vent, but an arm allows the charger a little distance from the vent. It's also a little bit stylish, a rarity for vent mounts. If you're using a Pixel or Samsung phone, we also like Peak Design's MagSafe phone cases.
Best Minimalist Car Phone Mount
Most people don't overwhelmingly want their car vent mount to be a defining feature in their car's interior. This Belkin takes this notion to the extreme. This silver and black air vent mount is minimalist, svelte, and—dare I say—almost classy. It grips phones surprisingly securely for a phone mount without feet to support the phone's bottom, according to WIRED reviewer Simon Hill, and you can rotate easily from portrait to landscape. There's also a handy rubber clip to hold charging cables in place. Just note that this will not be the best option for larger or heavier phones.
★ For larger phones: The Kenu Airframe Pro ($30) has a similar design but is built to accommodate thicker cases and larger phones, noted WIRED tester Simon Hill. The ball-and-socket joint allows 360-degree rotation and also lets you angle your phone for better viewing. It's a bit less sleek, however.
How I Test and Select Car Phone Mounts
Car phone mounts are and are not a sensitive technology. Bulky mounts can block your field of view while driving. And it's a genuine safety hazard if your car mount, or your phone, falls on the floor while you're driving down the freeway.
Every phone mount I and other WIRED testers recommend has been road-tested against this possibility, driven for hours on the road, and on long road trips, over sometimes bumpy roads. Often, I kept as many as eight devices at a time glued to my dash, windshield, and vents so that my car looked like a dollar-store communications center. For the most recent round of testing, this included multiple days of relatively humid, 90-degree Fahrenheit heat.
I pulled suction cups off of dashboards and windshields, over and over, to see if suction cups wore out the first time you had to move a device—or if the cups left residue on the windshield. I tested using multiple models of iPhone, a long folding Motorola Razr, and a large-model Nokia, onto each mount to see how it held up—with or without bulky cases.
I clamped each phone in and out repeatedly, to see how easy it is to remove a phone from the mount. I also turned each mount upside down and shook vigorously to see how violent I had to be to shake the phone loose from its mooring.
Where chargers were involved, I tested the charging capacity with ammeters and phone apps, as well as simply by marking how long it took to charge my phone compared to other chargers. I also tested the MagSafe charging speed vs. the speed if I'd just plugged the phone directly into my preferred USB car charger. (The USB always wins, for multiple reasons.)
For the most recent round of testing, I tested a dozen phone mounts during a sticky summer, selecting both best-selling and best-recommended mounts from both well-known brands and a new breed of hyper-specialized brands like Andobil and Andery that have made their name only on car phone mounts. My colleague Simon Hill likewise tested a dozen mounts in a previous round of testing.
Can Android Phones Use MagSafe and Qi2-Compatible Mounts?
MagSafe is a great technology for the more than half of cell phone owners in the US who use Apple products. The best phone mounts, with the fewest compromises, are pretty much all magnetic mounts.
But alas, most makers of Android phones have been more resistant to adding magnetic mounting capability. The Google Pixel 10 is an exception and offers built-in magnets and native Qi2-compatible charging support. Other phone makers, like Samsung, offer MagSafe-compatible cases for newer models like the Galaxy S26 series.
Some makers of MagSafe mounts offer little stick-on devices meant to affix to your non-magnetic phone. Don't bother with these; they don't work that well and don't stay affixed for long. If you'd like the convenience of a magnetic mount, you're going to have to get a MagSafe-compatible case for your phone. And for this, I refer you to WIRED's guide to the Best MagSafe Accessories.
Honorable Mentions
Belkin 15W MagSafe Mount for $80: This Belkin MagSafe charger and vent mount is an older device we've recommended previously as a top pick—with a secure magnet pad that offers 15-watt Qi2 charging. The mount positions itself in the air vent and blocks airflow a bit, but on summer days with the air-conditioner running, this positioning can help cool your phone while it charges. It's also a little bit sleek but also a bit on the spendy side for what it offers.
Andobil MagSafe Air Vent Mount for $37: This vent-mounted MagSafe device looks like a charger but isn't. The mount's broad, flat surface does stabilize the phone a bit. But in trade, it blocks airflow both to the phone and from the air vent. For these reasons, it's not really my favorite design. But the magnet is strong enough to hold the phone in place, and the vent mount is also stable.
iOttie iTap 3 Air Vent Holder for $16: This compact vent mount from iOttie is low-cost, and the MagSafe mount is strong enough. I can hold this thing upside down and shake it without dislodging my phone. But there's very little range of motion, and the phone can only be mounted where it'll block airflow from the vent. I also tend not to favor mounting mechanisms that use hooks, because it can make the mounts more difficult to remove when needed—though for unusual air vent geometries, the hook might be the only style of vent mount that works.
iOttie One Touch Dash and Windshield Mount for $28: This dash and windshield mount from iOttie was a favorite of WIRED tester Simon Hill when he tested it two years ago. But there's been a design update and some reports of durability issues, so until we test the newest model, I'm leaving this in the honorable mentions.
Vanmass Car Phone Holder for $40: Similar to the Andobil I recommend as a top pick, this Vanmass is a ball-socket mount with options for air vent or dashboard/windshield mounting. But it's a bit bulkier than the Andobil, and the air vent mount is a hook-based mount—which I tend to find more difficult to remove. The suction cup on the dash/windshield mount is ridiculously strong and is unllikely to dislodge even on hot days—and didn't leave residue when I removed it. But while Vanmass advertises “military-grade” tech, whatever this means for a phone mount, the plastic felt a bit flimsy, especially on a vacuum locking mechanism for the suction cup.
Bokilino Car Cup Mount for $16: This is a different sort of phone mount than most I tested: It affixes to a standard cup holder and holds up your phone like a liberty torch from atop a bendable gooseneck stem. This is all well and good when you're driving solo, notes WIRED reviewer Kat Merck, but during longer trips with family, it takes up a much-needed cup holder, and the stem can get in the way. In most cars, you'll have to look a bit too far away from the road to see the screen.
Not Recommended
Acer Gadget Car Phone Mount for $28: This little car mount from Acer mirrored the design of my top-pick Andery but fell far short on performance. The suction cup pretty much walked off the job after I removed and replaced it once, the magnet isn't as strong, and the mounting arm is shorter and doesn't rotate. There's no particular reason to buy it in a world where the Andery exists.
iOttie iTap 3 Dash and Windshield Mount for $25: MagSafe car phone mounts from iOttie have one chief merit: The magnet is strong and secure, unlikely to dislodge on even the bumpiest roads. But alas, the same cannot be said for the suction cup on this bulky dash and windshield mount, which gave up the ghost on a hot day.
Scosche Magic Mount for $13: This is maybe the most compact, low-cost MagSafe device I tested. Its S-branded design is both unobtrusive and winningly inscrutable: It looks like a talisman Jor-El might have brought back from Krypton. It's also the one with the weakest magnet. My iPhone lurched off at minor provocations.
iOttie Wireless 2 Qi Charging Phone Mount for $50: Don't mistake “Wireless 2 Qi Charger” for a Qi2 charger. A couple of years back, this MagSafe charging mount was a top pick for WIRED, but the charging is now a bit sluggish by modern standards.

articles.title: Giá iPhone 17 Pro Max chạm đáy chưa?
articles.text:
Giá bán của iPhone 17 Pro Max chỉ giảm nhẹ trong những ngày gần đây, mặc dù sản phẩm đang đi đến những ngày cuối của vòng đời.
Thông thường trong giai đoạn hè đến đầu mùa thu, các mẫu iPhone thường giảm giá mạnh để kích cầu do thị trường bước vào giai đoạn thấp điểm còn người dùng chờ đợi thông tin về iPhone phiên bản mới.
Tuy nhiên, điều đó không đúng với năm nay.
Trong khoảng 2-3 tháng gần đây, giá iPhone 17 Pro Max - phiên bản đắt nhất và hot nhất thị trường - gần như không giảm nhiều. Khảo sát tại các hệ thống bán lẻ, giá bán của iPhone 17 Pro Max phiên bản 256 GB có giá khoảng 34,2-34,6 triệu đồng, phiên bản 512 GB có giá 40,5-41,5 triệu đồng. So với thời điểm cách đây 1 tháng, giá bán chỉ giảm khoảng 500.000 đồng.
Nếu tìm mua trên các kênh thương mại điện tử, giá sản phẩm có thể tốt hơn nhờ áp các mã giảm giá sâu. Chẳng hạn, iPhone 17 Pro Max 256 GB sau khi áp mã giảm giá có thể về mức khoảng 32,5 triệu đồng. Thời gian giao hàng khoảng 1-3 ngày, cho thấy nguồn hàng trong các kho khá dồi dào.
Như vậy so với mức giá mở bán gần 1 năm trước (tháng 9/2025) là 38 triệu đồng, giá iPhone 17 Pro Max chỉ giảm khoảng 10% - mức giảm siêu thấp nếu so với các mẫu máy Android hoặc so với chính iPhone các năm gần đây.
Không riêng iPhone 17 Pro Max, các phiên bản khác như iPhone 17 Pro và 17 tiêu chuẩn cũng được giữ ở mức khá cao. Chẳng hạn, iPhone 17 Pro bản 256 GB có giá bán khoảng 31,5 triệu đồng – giảm 3,5 triệu so với thời điểm mở bán trong khi iPhone 17 tiêu chuẩn 128 GB hiện có giá 23 triệu – chỉ giảm 2 triệu đồng so với cách đây một năm.
Giá iPhone 17 Pro Max đã chạm đáy chưa?
Nhiều người mua iPhone thường chọn thời điểm cuối vòng đời hoặc khi model mới ra mắt để "xuống tiền" nhằm tiết kiệm chi phí. Câu hỏi đặt ra là giá iPhone 17 Pro Max hiện tại đã chạm đáy chưa.
Theo nhiều người am hiểu với thị trường iPhone, iPhone 17 Pro Max có thể giảm thêm nhưng sẽ khó giảm sâu bởi 2 yếu tố.
Thứ nhất, tình trạng thiếu hụt RAM kết hợp chi phí linh kiện tăng cao trên thị trường toàn cầu gần đây có thể sẽ đẩy giá iPhone 18 Pro Max (dự kiến ra mắt tháng 9 tới đây) lên cao. Apple đã tăng giá hàng loạt sản phẩm iPad, laptop và cố giữ cho iPhone 17 series không tăng giá để ổn định doanh số nhưng với iPhone 18, rất khó để nói trước điều gì.
Trong khi đó, Apple có xu hướng khai tử các phiên bản Pro và Pro Max của thế hệ cũ khi ra mắt thế hệ mới. tại Việt Nam, các phiên bản Pro và Pro Max thế hệ cũ thường sẽ hết hàng sau khoảng nửa năm model mới ra mắt. Với việc hàng tồn kho không quá nhiều, giá model mới có thể tăng mạnh thì việc người mua tìm đến các thế hệ cũ có thể tăng cao, từ đó thậm chí dẫn đến tình trạng tăng giá chứ không hề giảm.
Thực tế thị trường năm ngoái cho thấy, iPhone 15 Pro Max giảm giá trước thời điểm 16 Pro Max ra mắt nhưng sau đó có giai đoạn tăng khá nhiều, một phần cũng do nguyên nhân tương tự.

articles.title: Apple M5 Ultra vs M3 Ultra: What's changed? - Engadget
articles.text:
Apple M5 Ultra vs M3 Ultra: What's changed?
Here's how the company's most powerful chip ever stacks up with the previous generation.
Apple just launched the new M5 Ultra for the latest Mac Studio and as you'd expect, it's the fastest consumer processor the company has ever built. But how much speedier is it than its predecessor, the M3 Ultra? Let's dive in and see how Apple's latest super silicon measures up.
If you've followed Apple's Ultra chip family so far, you've probably noticed that it has skipped the M4 and M6 generations and only come out as M1 Ultra, M2 Ultra, M3 Ultra and now M5 Ultra versions. The reason for that (and the delay compared to Apple's other chips) is because of the complexity — they're effectively two processors mated together using Apple's "Ultrafusion" bridge technology.
This chip fusion design has carried forward to the M5 Ultra, but there's a key change from before. The M3 Ultra married two M3 Max dies with over 10,000 high speed connections, according to Apple. However, the M5 Ultra fuses two dual-die M5 Max chips to form an all-new quad-die architecture, a first for Apple silicon. The new chip also has six times the connection density and boosts the interconnection speed to 4.4TB/s, up from the M3 Ultra's 2.5TB/s interconnection speed. These faster speeds between chip dies allows for improved efficiency and faster performance.
The M5 Ultra offers up to 36 processing cores in the top version, up from 32 before. Those include 12 super cores and 24 performance cores, compared to the M3 Ultra's 24 performance and eight "efficiency" cores. Those extra and faster cores help it deliver 25 percent faster single-threaded performance and up to 30 percent faster multithreaded performance. Along with the extra compute power, Apple also promises "industry leading energy efficiency," though it didn't provide any numbers to back that up.
Both chips support up to an incredible 512GB of unified memory. However, the M5 Ultra bumps unified memory performance by 50 percent over the M3 Ultra to 1.2TB/s, letting you "store huge datasets entirely in local memory, increase the tokens-per-second speed, and run huge LLMs with hundreds of billions of parameters entirely on device," Apple says. Given current high memory prices, though, the top 512GB configuration (coming in October)will likely cost around $15,000.
Both the M5 Ultra and M3 Ultra have 80 GPU cores, but Apple has redesigned those to improve graphics and AI performance. There's now a Neural Accelerator in each core that boosts AI compute speeds up to 4.5 times compared to the M3 Ultra. The GPU also includes Apple's latest shader core with second-generation Dynamic Caching, plus hardware-accelerated mesh shading and third-generation ray tracing, delivering up to a 40 percent speed boost compared to the M3 Ultra.
And for content creators, the M5 Ultra comes with an updated Media Engine with four ProRes encode and decode engines, along with hardware-accelerated AV1, H.264 and HEVC codecs. The boosted Media Engine speeds will allow you to play 33 streams of 8K 30 fps ProRes video at once, compared to 24 before.
It will be easy to connect fast storage, as the M5 Ultra pro supports 120Gbps Thunderbolt 5 connection speeds, just like the M3 Pro. And the new chip now supports PCIe Gen 6 internal SSD architecture (updated from PCIe Gen 5 before) that it says offers "industry-leading read and write speeds for rapid project loading, file transfers, and loading huge LLMs." That technology, previously only found in data centers, offers speeds up to 128GB/s for supported x16 lane devices. It's currently overkill, though, as the world's fastest SSD from Micron tops out at 28GB/s.
Apple gave a few examples of performance uplift compared to the M3 Ultra:
- Up to 3.3x faster CopyCat ML training performance in Foundry Nuke when compared to Mac Studio with M3 Ultra.
- Up to 4x faster LLM prompt processing in LM Studio when compared to Mac Studio with M3 Ultra.
- Up to 4.3x faster text-to-image LLM performance when compared to Mac Studio with M3 Ultra.
- Up to 1.7x faster scene rendering performance in Maxon Redshift when compared to Mac Studio with M3 Ultra.
As mentioned, the Ultra processors are a generation and M-number behind Apple's other chips, so they use older process technology. The M5 Ultra uses TSMC's third-generation 3-nanometer process, while the new M6 is built using 2nm technology. However, the M5 Ultra's third-gen 3nm process is considerably more efficient and performant than the M3 Ultra, since the latter is built using TSMC's older first-gen 3nm process.
Apple's product prices have gone up across the board (thanks AI data centers) and the new Mac Studio is no exception. If you're fortunate enough to already own an M3 Ultra-powered version, you likely won't need to upgrade to the M5 Ultra unless you're a serious power user with some cash. If you're in the market for a new machine, though, get ready to cry: the M5 Ultra-powered Mac Studios with 96GB of RAM will start at $5,499, compared to $3,999 for the base 96GB M3 Ultra Mac Studio when it first launched last year — a $1,500 increase.

articles.title: That fake Grand Theft Auto VI demo is actually just malware | TechCrunch
articles.text:
In the long wait for the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI, an open-world game about crime, some in the gaming community are being targeted by cybercriminals in the real world.
Fans are still waiting for the game more than a decade after the release of GTA 5, which sold more copies than any game ever, except for Minecraft. Now, after multiple GTA 6 delays and with some fans desperate for any scrap of news, hackers are using the cover as a perfect opportunity to target eager gamers.
Cybercriminals have created fake websites impersonating Rockstar, the developer behind GTA 6. These websites advertise a playable GTA 6 demo — but no legitimate demo exists. Once the unsuspecting gamer clicks the “Play Now” button, they download a file that looks like a game installer, but is actually malware, according to the cybersecurity company Malwarebytes.
The malware is an information stealer that is designed to find and take a victim’s passwords, cookies, and logged-in sessions stored in their web browser. These attacks can in some cases allow hackers to log in as if they were the account holder, even when protected by multi-factor authentication.
After multiple delays, GTA 6 is expected to release on November 19, 2026. On Thursday, Netflix will air an extended look at the game, which could perhaps answer some questions about the legitimacy of various leaks.
A relevant reminder as always: Don’t download stuff if you aren’t sure it comes from a reliable source.

articles.title: Brazil fined TikTok over data from users who never logged in
articles.text:
Brazil has fined TikTok’s owner over the way it handled children’s data, and the ruling covers people who never had an account.
The National Data Protection Agency imposed a penalty of 153.7 million reais on ByteDance on Tuesday, worth about $29.9m. It cited irregularities in the processing of data belonging to children and adolescents.
TikTok breached data privacy law across both logged-in accounts and guest browsing sessions, the regulator said in its ruling. It collected and processed young users’ personal information without a valid legal basis or adequate safeguards.
Mauricio Savarese reported the decision for the Associated Press. Agence France-Presse carried the agency’s figures.
The guest-session finding is the part that travels
Most child-safety enforcement to date has turned on accounts. Regulators ask how old a user said they were, what the platform did to check, and what settings applied afterwards.
Brazil has gone further. Its regulator found that the data problem existed for people browsing without signing in at all.
That reading does not depend on age verification working. It treats the collection itself as the breach, whoever is at the other end.
What TikTok has to do
The agency ordered ByteDance to delete the data it collected in violation of the rules. It also told the company to produce a plan for protecting minors better.
TikTok has committed to a compliance plan, the agency said. The platform will have to apply stricter privacy settings automatically to accounts belonging to under-16s.
It must also strengthen parental supervision systems and put in place stricter content filters.
ByteDance has 10 days to appeal. It did not comment to the AP and did not respond to AFP.
What the ruling does not do
Brazil has not suspended TikTok, blocked it or restricted what it publishes. The remedies all concern data and settings.
That is a narrower action than the one the first lady called for, and a narrower one than the country has taken before against a platform.
It is also the kind of order a company can comply with and keep operating, which is why the appeal is worth watching rather than assuming.
The same regulator moved on Discord this month
This is the second time in three weeks that Brazil’s data protection agency has acted against a platform over child safety.
It told Discord to suspend livestreaming after the death of a 13-year-old girl. Discord appealed on Monday and the agency has that appeal under review.
The two wire accounts differ slightly on that order. AFP describes the agency as having ordered the suspension, and the AP describes it as a recommendation.
An agency that was issuing recommendations three weeks ago is issuing fines now, whichever word applies.
Brazil has been building to this
A recent Brazilian law requires platforms to link accounts held by under-16s to a parent’s account, and to verify how old users are.
The country has form on enforcement. X was blocked in Brazil for 40 days in 2024 until it complied with Supreme Court orders to remove accounts accused of spreading disinformation.
Regulators there have also had to deal with newer problems. Brazil banned Jair Bolsonaro from speaking during an election, and his AI avatar spoke anyway.
President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s government and the Supreme Court have both pushed to regulate how minors use the internet, with mixed results. The first lady, Rosangela Lula da Silva, said on 6 August that TikTok should be taken offline.
Where this sits against Europe
The European Commission charged TikTok in July with failing to protect children’s privacy under the Digital Services Act. That case is still open and no fine has landed.
Brazil has reached a penalty and a remedy first, on a narrower legal basis. The DSA case is about systemic risk assessment, while this one is about a lawful basis for processing data, which is the same test European regulators apply under the GDPR.
The practical difference matters for anyone watching Brussels. A data protection authority can fine a company for how it collects information without having to prove the design of the product caused harm.
European regulators have the same instrument to hand. Every EU country has a data protection authority, and the lawful-basis test Brazil applied is written into the GDPR.
Every jurisdiction is trying something different
Australia, Canada and Indonesia are all working on similar rules. TikTok and YouTube cut 4.7 million under-16 accounts in Indonesia in June.
New Zealand joined the push to keep under-16s off social media on Monday. The UK has proposed a curfew, Australia has an outright ban, and Hong Kong educators want one.
The approaches are not converging. Bans, curfews, parental linking, age assurance and data protection fines all target the same problem through different law.
It landed on the same day as Oakland
A former Meta data scientist told a jury in California on Tuesday that Instagram had rejected a default setting for a teen safety tool, because the cost to the app’s core metrics was not desirable.
The two cases test different things. The US trial is about whether a company lied about a feature. Brazil did not have to argue about statements at all.
It asked whether there was a lawful basis for holding the data, decided there was not, and set a price.
What happens next
The first thing is the appeal. ByteDance has until early September, and its response will show whether it treats a $29.9m penalty as a cost or as a precedent worth fighting.
The second is the deletion order. Deleting data collected from guest sessions is harder than deleting an account, because there is no account to point at.
The third is whether other data protection authorities read the guest-browsing finding and try it. That is the part of this ruling with the longest reach, and it is the part TikTok has the most reason to contest.

articles.title: Tại sao Bluetooth lại mang tên một vị vua Viking?
articles.text:
Điều thú vị nằm ở chỗ các kỹ sư không chọn tên này chỉ vì nó lạ.
Mỗi ngày có hàng tỷ thiết bị sử dụng Bluetooth để kết nối với nhau. Tai nghe, điện thoại, máy tính, ô tô hay đồng hồ thông minh đều có thể giao tiếp không dây nhờ công nghệ này. Ít người biết cái tên Bluetooth không phải một thuật ngữ công nghệ, cũng không phải viết tắt của một cụm từ tiếng Anh. Nó bắt nguồn từ tên của một vị vua Viking sống cách đây hơn 1.000 năm.
Người đó là Harald “Bluetooth” Gormsson, một vị vua Đan Mạch nổi tiếng với việc thống nhất Đan Mạch và Na Uy vào năm 958. Theo Bluetooth SIG, Harald còn được biết đến với một chiếc răng bị hỏng có màu xanh đậm hoặc xanh xám, từ đó xuất hiện biệt danh Bluetooth.
Điều thú vị nằm ở chỗ các kỹ sư không chọn tên này chỉ vì nó lạ.
Năm 1996, Intel, Ericsson và Nokia cùng bàn về việc chuẩn hóa một công nghệ vô tuyến tầm ngắn, với mục tiêu giúp những thiết bị và ngành công nghiệp vốn đang sử dụng các hệ thống khác nhau có thể kết nối với nhau. Tại cuộc gặp này, Jim Kardach của Intel đề xuất Bluetooth làm tên mã tạm thời.
Ý tưởng khá đơn giản. Harald Bluetooth từng được biết đến với việc thống nhất các vùng lãnh thổ ở Scandinavia. Công nghệ mới cũng được kỳ vọng làm điều tương tự với thế giới công nghệ, kết nối ngành máy tính với ngành điện thoại di động thông qua một chuẩn không dây duy nhất.
Tên Bluetooth khi đó hoàn toàn không được định dùng lâu dài. Các bên từng cân nhắc những cái tên mang tính kỹ thuật hơn như RadioWire hoặc PAN, viết tắt của Personal Area Networking. PAN từng là phương án được ưu tiên, cho tới khi quá trình kiểm tra cho thấy cái tên này đã xuất hiện hàng chục nghìn lần trên Internet. Việc kiểm tra thương hiệu cho RadioWire cũng không thể hoàn tất kịp thời điểm ra mắt.
Kết quả là cái tên tưởng như chỉ dùng tạm thời lại trở thành lựa chọn duy nhất. Bluetooth nhanh chóng được sử dụng rộng rãi trong ngành trước khi bất kỳ phương án thay thế nào có thể được đưa ra.
Đến đây vẫn còn một chi tiết thú vị hơn. Logo Bluetooth không phải một biểu tượng được thiết kế ngẫu nhiên. Nó là sự kết hợp của hai chữ rune Bắc Âu thuộc hệ Younger Futhark, Hagall và Bjarkan, tương ứng với các chữ cái đầu trong tên Harald Bluetooth. Hai ký tự được ghép lại thành biểu tượng mà hàng triệu người nhận ra trên các thiết bị điện tử ngày nay.
Nói cách khác, mỗi lần nhìn thấy biểu tượng Bluetooth trên chiếc điện thoại hay tai nghe, người dùng thực chất đang nhìn thấy một dấu vết của lịch sử Viking được đưa thẳng vào ngành công nghệ hiện đại./
Vũ Hoàng

articles.title: The County Prosecutors Who Became ICE Informants
articles.text:
This story was produced in partnership with Injustice Watch, a nonprofit newsroom in Chicago focused on the court system.
Rolando Perez Samayoa had come to the US in 2023 seeking safety. Fleeing violence in Mexico, he’d first planned to make a life in Alabama but had been told that Illinois would protect immigrants like him. “There’s some kind of law there,” he said. “It’s supposed to be a sanctuary.”
He was referring to the state’s 2017 TRUST Act, which was meant to keep local law enforcement out of federal deportation efforts. Samayoa made his way to southern Illinois and found work cleaning a factory. After a DUI arrest in Marion County last October, Samayoa said, he attended his hearings—a fact confirmed by court records.
In late January, John Christeson, an assistant state’s attorney in the office prosecuting the case, emailed an agent with Homeland Security Investigations, a division of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement, about Samayoa. The message included his date of birth, an upcoming court date, and where he lived: Centralia, Illinois.
“Ok, we’ll take care of it, thank you,” the federal agent, Sergio Fulgencio, wrote back minutes later. Two days later, he wanted to know more: “Do you have any reports on this guy?”
Christeson sent him the police report and related tickets. Three weeks later, federal agents apprehended Samayoa outside his home. They hauled off his 17-year-old son, too.
The exchange is among dozens of emails reviewed by Injustice Watch that reveal a pattern of consequential collaboration between county prosecutors and federal immigration agencies across Illinois during the first 15 months of President Donald Trump’s second term.
State’s attorneys offices in 1 out of every 6 Illinois counties acted as valuable assets of federal immigration enforcement, sharing sensitive personal data about the people they were prosecuting without criminal warrants, public disclosure, or legislative oversight and with no accounting of how often it happened or who was affected.
Sometimes, prosecutors volunteered information on their own. Other times, they simply answered when Department of Homeland Security agents came calling. The correspondence crossed party lines and included everyone from paralegals to elected state’s attorneys. The collaboration typically happened without the knowledge of defendants or their attorneys.
The TRUST Act bars police and other agencies from helping federal agents deport people absent a federal criminal warrant. But the law doesn’t squarely answer whether prosecutors and their staff are bound by those same restrictions.
Since Trump took office for the second time, his administration has ramped up immigration enforcement, detention, and deportation, and ICE has visibly displayed its enforcement at worksites, front yards, and courthouses. In response, states including New York have joined Illinois and more than a dozen others in barring local police and sheriffs from helping with federal immigration enforcement. But the scale of prosecutor collaboration in Illinois—which is one of the largest sanctuary states and is often cited as a national model—raises questions about the limitations of state laws to protect immigrants.
Injustice Watch filed Freedom of Information Act requests with all 102 Illinois state’s attorney’s offices and drew on records from federal and circuit courts. Together, those internal emails and case files ran more than 5,000 pages. The documents reveal that prosecutors shared much more than just names. Their emails contain photographs. Home addresses. The date and time a defendant was due in court or set to leave jail—the exact window for ICE to make an arrest.
Eleven offices didn’t respond; some produced records only after Injustice Watch sued them under FOIA. The rest remain in litigation.
And the written record may be only part of the story. Messages with phrases like “Thank you for taking my call” point to conversations no records requests could follow.
None of it was inevitable. Dozens of Illinois county prosecutors, faced with the same federal pressure, claimed they had no record of contact with ICE, and at least one made a point of shutting it out—suggesting every act of collaboration was a choice.
And the choices had consequences: People flagged to ICE were detained and deported, tearing families apart.
DHS did not answer questions about how its agents work with local officials in Illinois.
Antonio Gutierrez, who cofounded the advocacy group Organized Communities Against Deportations, was among those who pushed for the TRUST Act. Residents wanted “to trust in local police, in local prosecutors, in the criminal justice system, to be fully separated from immigration and deportation enforcement,” Gutierrez said.
The records revealed in Injustice Watch’s investigation, Gutierrez said, prove that trust was never warranted.
The Ones Who Were Willing
Twenty minutes after flagging Samayoa, Marion County’s Christeson emailed Fulgencio again.
“I’ve got another potential,” he wrote, flagging a man with a local warrant who had been arrested on an unrelated charge in Missouri.
Fulgencio replied that agents were already tracking the man on a civil removal order—a deportation order from an immigration court—and asked whether the county warrant should take priority.
“Our warrant will not take priority over removal,” Christeson answered.
Fulgencio wrote back just 34 minutes later: “He’s in ICE Custody awaiting removal.”
Christeson didn’t respond to questions about his correspondence with Fulgencio, nor did his boss, Marion County State’s Attorney Tim Hudspeth.
Criminal cases offer protections that immigration proceedings don’t: Prosecutors must prove guilt beyond a reasonable doubt, and attorneys are appointed to defendants who can’t afford one. Removal proceedings are civil: There’s no right to an appointed lawyer, and the government can establish deportability on “clear and convincing evidence,” a lower legal standard.
Spencer Reynolds, an attorney with the NAACP Legal Defense Fund and a former Department of Homeland Security lawyer, said that because deportation is an easier path than prosecution, some local officials might be tempted to use it to “clear their docket”—a move that “risks undermining the rights people have in the criminal proceeding context.” Once a defendant is turned over to ICE, the criminal case—and the protections it affords the accused—fall away.
In several counties, prosecutors reached out only once or twice. Some local prosecutor’s offices did nothing more than ask immigration officials whether a defendant was already in federal custody but may have put the person on ICE’s radar in the asking.
According to documents reviewed by Injustice Watch, contact happened more often in DuPage County in Chicago’s western suburbs, where 1 in 5 residents were born abroad. Staff there contacted federal immigration agents more than any other prosecutor’s office in the state. Staffers answered ICE’s requests for information and offered specific cases for federal agents to pursue.
In April 2025, for example, a Customs and Border Protection officer based at O’Hare International Airport asked an assistant prosecutor for records tied to a voter fraud investigation. The request was an administrative subpoena—issued by DHS, not by a judge. On its own it carried little weight: If the office refused, DHS would have to go to federal court and attempt to enforce it.
Ninety minutes later, the prosecutor sent the voting records of two county residents.
DuPage State’s Attorney Bob Berlin said his office reviewed the subpoena like any other before producing the records CBP sought. Its other contacts with immigration agents, he said, were permitted under the TRUST Act’s criminal investigation carve-out, which allows cooperation with federal agencies—including Homeland Security—in such investigations.
Sometimes, the collaboration crossed county lines.
In central Illinois, Menard County State’s Attorney Gwendolyn Thomas contacted federal immigration agents on at least five occasions, often asking whether a defendant was “on a deportation list” in order to assess flight risk, and sometimes sharing details about the men she was prosecuting, including when one might be released from jail.
She also pointed colleagues in neighboring Cass and Mason counties to Homeland Security investigator Kevin Parks. Prosecutors subsequently wrote to Parks on their own, telling him Thomas had shared his contact information.
Cass County State’s Attorney Craig Miller—who shared information about three defendants with federal agents—declined to comment. Thomas didn’t respond to questions about her communications with agents or about steering other prosecutors to Parks.
Mason County State’s Attorney Zachary Bryant told Injustice Watch that the information his office had received from Homeland Security “was helpful in obtaining appropriate identification for purposes of obtaining a valid criminal history for the defendant,” even though records show Parks shared information regarding the defendant’s immigration history, not her criminal history. Bryant did not respond to questions about the discrepancy.
None of the state’s attorneys who responded to Injustice Watch’s questions described the contact they and their staff had made as a mistake or the work of a rogue employee; like DuPage County’s Berlin, most defended their practices outright.
“It is very common that information is shared between agencies in the criminal justice system, including those in law enforcement,” wrote Kendall County State’s Attorney Eric Weis, whose office sent a man’s records to a Detroit ICE office for use in immigration court proceedings.
In Kane County, where staffers asked Customs and Border Protection to identify three people through facial recognition, State’s Attorney Jamie Mosser called it “a standard investigatory technique used throughout all of law enforcement.”
The Ones Who Said No
In response to records requests, more than half of Illinois state’s attorneys offices said they had no record of contact with ICE since Trump returned to office. Some offices chose not to collaborate out of internal practice, some out of a commitment to community trust.
In Lake County, State’s Attorney Eric Rinehart spent months hardening his office against immigration enforcement. He circulated the Illinois attorney general’s guidance on complying with the TRUST Act to police chiefs and told the county’s public defender to report any TRUST Act violations, adding that he not only enforced the law, he “happen[ed] to agree with it such that I hope it is widely followed in letter and spirit.”
“When people are afraid to come to court, for any reason,” he wrote to state lawmakers in October, “we cannot make our communities safe, we cannot find the truth, and we cannot achieve justice.”
Rinehart also issued a written policy barring ICE officials from the private areas of his office without a warrant signed by a judge.
In southern Illinois, Jackson County treated questions from federal agents the way they would any other: as FOIA requests, answered with redactions under the state’s public records law.
Unprecedented
Illinois has made repeated promises to its residents about the way it treats immigrants.
Then-governor Bruce Rauner, a Republican, signed the TRUST Act with bipartisan support at a packed restaurant in Little Village, the Chicago neighborhood at the heart of the city’s Mexican community, months after Trump first took office in 2017 promising mass deportations. Among the attendees were law enforcement officials who wanted to assure the public that immigrants had no reason to fear contacting the police.
In 2021, Governor JB Pritzker called Illinois “the most welcoming state in the United States.” In June 2025, he flew to Washington to defend his position before a hostile House committee. In December, as ICE swept people up outside hearings, he also signed a law in Little Village, this one barring civil immigration arrests within 1,000 feet of a courthouse. The idea that the Trump administration would keep people from attending court, he said at the signing, “boggles the mind.”
But the courthouse law was written to stop the agent waiting on the sidewalk, not the prosecutor inside.
Nearly all the defense attorneys whose clients appear in the records obtained by Injustice Watch said they had no idea prosecutors were sharing case information with federal immigration agents. They spoke on the condition of anonymity, several citing concern about straining relationships with the prosecutors they face in court, others pointing to cases that are still pending.
Legal scholars described the collaboration between federal immigration agents and local prosecutors as unprecedented.
“I cannot recall a single instance in my past practice where an individual within the state’s attorney’s office shared information with ICE,” said University of Kentucky assistant law professor Matthew Boaz.
Still, he said in an email, “the sentiment of the TRUST Act—separating state/local criminal law enforcement from federal civil immigration enforcement—would seem to include any actor within the criminal legal system.”
Prosecutors themselves couldn’t agree on whether the TRUST Act applied to them.
Some said their offices are bound by it. The act covers law enforcement agencies; DuPage County’s Berlin said that includes him and his staff.
“The State’s Attorney’s Office is charged with enforcement of state, county, and municipal laws,” he said. “Therefore, the law applies to my office.”
Others said the law doesn’t reach them. Lake County’s Rinehart said his office doesn’t arrest or detain people, so it isn’t a law enforcement agency as defined by the act. Yet Rinehart said his office declines to collaborate with federal immigration enforcement regardless.
These two offices staked out the clearest positions, landing on opposite sides of the question—and on opposite ends of the spectrum of collaboration. Berlin said his office was bound by the TRUST Act, but it contacted federal immigration officials more than any other. Rinehart said his office wasn’t bound by it, yet shut ICE out entirely. (Neither office tracks its contact with ICE. While police departments and sheriff’s offices must file annual TRUST Act compliance reports, state’s attorneys aren’t required to do so.)
Illinois Attorney General Kwame Raoul, the state’s chief legal officer, didn’t resolve the question.
“Applying the TRUST Act in practice requires state and local enforcement to navigate complex interactions in circumstances that are not always clear-cut,” he said in a statement, without answering whether county prosecutors are bound by the law he enforces.
Pritzker didn’t respond to questions about whether the TRUST Act binds prosecutors, whether the state should track their contacts with ICE, or whether Illinois has kept its promises to its residents.
For Samayoa, the question of whom the law binds is beside the point.
Whatever idea he had about Illinois being a sanctuary ended in February, when ICE agents descended on him in his front yard as he was stepping out to grab a belated birthday dinner. He said eight agents pointed their guns at his teen son, who was trying to reach him as ICE moved in.
“Everything was going smoothly until his 17-year-old son thought he would help his dad out by trying to run over the agents,” Homeland Security’s Fulgencio wrote to Marion County’s Christeson after the incident. “Ended up damaging a vehicle. So now [his son’s] going with him.”
Samayoa denied that his son tried to run over the agents. DHS defended the way its agents handled the arrest.
“ICE law enforcement officers are trained to use the minimum amount of force necessary to resolve dangerous situations to prioritize the safety of the public and our officers,” a spokesperson said in a statement. “Officers are highly trained in de-escalation tactics and regularly receive ongoing use of force training.”
Samayoa and his son were taken to St. Louis, where he said he felt pressured to agree to leave the country rather than fight his case. He directed his son to do the same. The Department of Homeland Security confirmed both father and son “accepted a voluntary departure.” Within hours, both were on a plane to Texas.
After one night in an El Paso hotel, Samayoa said, he and his son were escorted across the border into Ciudad Juarez, where he destroyed all immigration paperwork he had with him—vowing to never return to the US. DHS confirmed both were removed from the US on Feb. 25.
Father and son spent time in a shelter before scraping together bus fare to their native state of Chiapas. Back in Illinois, the rest of the family had to raise their own fare south; two months passed before they were all together again.
When Injustice Watch reached Samayoa, he said he didn’t know that a prosecutor had shared information about him with federal immigration authorities before the raid. He said he’d warn the community he left behind in Illinois: Showing up for prosecutors could mean showing up for ICE.
